tools.name: PowerShell
tools.description:
Executes a given PowerShell command with optional timeout. Working directory persists between commands; shell state (variables, functions) does not.

IMPORTANT: This tool is for terminal operations via PowerShell: git, npm, docker, and PS cmdlets. DO NOT use it for file operations (reading, writing, editing, searching, finding files) - use the specialized tools for this instead.

PowerShell edition: Windows PowerShell 5.1 (powershell.exe)
   - Pipeline chain operators `&&` and `||` are NOT available — they cause a parser error. To run B only if A succeeds: `A; if ($?) { B }`. To chain unconditionally: `A; B`.
   - Ternary (`?:`), null-coalescing (`??`), and null-conditional (`?.`) operators are NOT available. Use `if/else` and explicit `$null -eq` checks instead.
   - Avoid `2>&1` on native executables. In 5.1, redirecting a native command's stderr inside PowerShell wraps each line in an ErrorRecord (NativeCommandError) and sets `$?` to `$false` even when the exe returned exit code 0. stderr is already captured for you — don't redirect it.
   - `>`, `>>`, and `Out-File` usually default to UTF-8 (with BOM) in this environment, but `Set-Content`/`Add-Content` still default to the system ANSI codepage — when writing a file other tools will read, pass `-Encoding utf8` explicitly to `Out-File`/`Set-Content`.
   - `ConvertFrom-Json` returns a PSCustomObject, not a hashtable. `-AsHashtable` is not available.

Before executing the command, please follow these steps:

1. Directory Verification:
   - If the command will create new directories or files, first use `Get-ChildItem` (or `ls`) to verify the parent directory exists and is the correct location

2. Command Execution:
   - Always quote file paths that contain spaces with double quotes
   - Capture the output of the command.

PowerShell Syntax Notes:
   - Variables use $ prefix: $myVar = "value"
   - Escape character is backtick (`), not backslash
   - Use Verb-Noun cmdlet naming: Get-ChildItem, Set-Location, New-Item, Remove-Item
   - Common aliases: ls (Get-ChildItem), cd (Set-Location), cat (Get-Content), rm (Remove-Item)
   - Pipe operator | works similarly to bash but passes objects, not text
   - Use Select-Object, Where-Object, ForEach-Object for filtering and transformation
   - String interpolation: "Hello $name" or "Hello $($obj.Property)"
   - Registry access uses PSDrive prefixes: `HKLM:\SOFTWARE\...`, `HKCU:\...` — NOT raw `HKEY_LOCAL_MACHINE\...`
   - Environment variables: read with `$env:NAME`, set with `$env:NAME = "value"` (NOT `Set-Variable` or bash `export`)
   - Call native exe with spaces in path via call operator: `& "C:\Program Files\App\app.exe" arg1 arg2`

Unix commands that DO NOT exist in PowerShell — use the equivalent instead:
   - head / tail → `Get-Content file -TotalCount N` / `-Tail N`; piped: `| Select-Object -First N` / `-Last N`
   - which → `(Get-Command name).Source`
   - touch → `if (-not (Test-Path path)) { New-Item -ItemType File path }` (NEVER use `New-Item -Force` on a file — it truncates existing content)
   - wc -l → `(Get-Content file | Measure-Object -Line).Lines`
   - mkdir -p → `New-Item -ItemType Directory -Force path` (`-p` is not a PowerShell flag)
   - rm -rf → `Remove-Item -Recurse -Force path`
   - ln -s → `New-Item -ItemType SymbolicLink -Path link -Target target`
   - chmod / chown → not applicable on Windows; use `icacls` only if ACL changes are required
   - 2>/dev/null → `2>$null` (but stderr is captured for you — usually unnecessary)
   - VAR=x cmd → `$env:VAR = 'x'; cmd` (PowerShell has no inline env-var prefix)
   - Bash control flow (`if [ -f x ]`, `for x in *`, backtick ``cmd`` substitution) is a parser error — use `if (Test-Path x)`, `foreach ($x in ...)`, `$(cmd)`

Exit-code note: `-ErrorAction SilentlyContinue` suppresses error OUTPUT but the cmdlet failure still causes this tool to report exit 1. To make a cmdlet failure truly non-fatal, promote it to terminating and swallow it: `try { Cmdlet ... -ErrorAction Stop } catch {}` (without `-ErrorAction Stop`, non-terminating errors skip the `catch` and still exit 1).

Interactive and blocking commands (this tool runs with -NonInteractive and stdin attached to the null device — console prompts read EOF or error immediately; GUI prompts can still block until timeout):
   - NEVER use `Read-Host`, `Get-Credential`, `Out-GridView`, `$Host.UI.PromptForChoice`, or `pause`
   - Destructive cmdlets (`Remove-Item`, `Stop-Process`, `Clear-Content`, etc.) may prompt for confirmation. Add `-Confirm:$false` when you intend the action to proceed. Use `-Force` for read-only/hidden items.
   - Never use `git rebase -i`, `git add -i`, or other commands that open an interactive editor

Passing multiline strings (commit messages, file content) to native executables:
   - Use a single-quoted here-string so PowerShell does not expand `$` or backticks inside. The closing `'@` MUST be at column 0 (no leading whitespace) on its own line — indenting it is a parse error:
<example>
git commit -m @'
Commit message here.
Second line with $literal dollar signs.
'@
</example>
   - Use `@'...'@` (single-quoted, literal) not `@"..."@` (double-quoted, interpolated) unless you need variable expansion
   - For arguments containing `-`, `@`, or other characters PowerShell parses as operators, use the stop-parsing token: `git log --% --format=%H`

Usage notes:
  - The command argument is required.
  - You can specify an optional timeout in milliseconds (up to 600000ms / 10 minutes for a foreground command). If not specified, commands will timeout after 120000ms (2 minutes).
  - It is very helpful if you write a clear, concise description of what this command does.
  - If the output exceeds 30000 characters, output will be truncated before being returned to you.
  - You can use the `run_in_background` parameter to run the command in the background. Only use this if you don't need the result immediately and are OK being notified when the command completes later. You do not need to check the output right away - you'll be notified when it finishes.
  - Avoid using PowerShell to run commands that have dedicated tools, unless explicitly instructed:
    - File search: Use Glob (NOT Get-ChildItem -Recurse)
    - Content search: Use Grep (NOT Select-String)
    - Read files: Use Read (NOT Get-Content)
    - Edit files: Use Edit
    - Write files: Use Write (NOT Set-Content/Out-File)
    - Communication: Output text directly (NOT Write-Output/Write-Host)
  - When issuing multiple commands:
    - If the commands are independent and can run in parallel, make multiple PowerShell tool calls in a single message.
    - If the commands depend on each other and must run sequentially, chain them in a single PowerShell call (see edition-specific chaining syntax above).
    - Use `;` only when you need to run commands sequentially but don't care if earlier commands fail.
    - DO NOT use newlines to separate commands (newlines are ok in quoted strings and here-strings)
  - Do NOT prefix commands with `cd` or `Set-Location` -- the working directory is already set to the correct project directory automatically.
  - Avoid unnecessary `Start-Sleep` commands:
    - Do not sleep between commands that can run immediately — just run them.
    - If your command is long running and you would like to be notified when it finishes — simply run your command using `run_in_background`. There is no need to sleep in this case.
    - Do not retry failing commands in a sleep loop — diagnose the root cause or consider an alternative approach.
    - If waiting for a background task you started with `run_in_background`, you will be notified when it completes — do not poll.
    - If you must poll an external process, use a check command rather than sleeping first.
    - If you must sleep, keep the duration short to avoid blocking the user.
  - For git commands:
    - Prefer to create a new commit rather than amending an existing commit.
    - Before running destructive operations (e.g., git reset --hard, git push --force, git checkout --), consider whether there is a safer alternative that achieves the same goal. Only use destructive operations when they are truly the best approach.
    - Never skip hooks (--no-verify) or bypass signing (--no-gpg-sign, -c commit.gpgsign=false) unless the user has explicitly asked for it. If a hook fails, investigate and fix the underlying issue.

tools.name: Read
tools.description:
Reads a file from the local filesystem.

- `file_path` must be an absolute path.
- Reads up to 2000 lines by default.
- When you already know which part of the file you need, only read that part. This can be important for larger files.
- Results are returned using cat -n format, with line numbers starting at 1
- Reads images (PNG, JPG, …) and presents them visually. Reads PDFs via the `pages` parameter (e.g. "1-5", max 20 pages/request; required for PDFs over 10 pages). Reads Jupyter notebooks (.ipynb) as cells with outputs.
- Reading a directory, a missing file, or an empty file returns an error or system reminder rather than content.
- Do NOT re-read a file you just edited to verify — Edit/Write would have errored if the change failed, and the harness tracks file state for you.

tools.name: ScheduleWakeup
tools.description:
Schedule when to resume work in /loop dynamic mode — the user invoked /loop without an interval, asking you to self-pace iterations of a specific task.

Do NOT schedule a short-interval wakeup to poll for background work you started — when harness-tracked work finishes, you are re-invoked automatically, so polling is wasted. Instead schedule a long fallback (1200s+) so the loop survives if the work hangs or never notifies. The exception is external work the harness cannot track (a CI run, a deploy, a remote queue) — there, pick a delay matched to how fast that state actually changes.

Pass the same /loop prompt back via `prompt` each turn so the next firing repeats the task. For an autonomous /loop (no user prompt), pass the literal sentinel `<<autonomous-loop-dynamic>>` as `prompt` instead — the runtime resolves it back to the autonomous-loop instructions at fire time. (There is a similar `<<autonomous-loop>>` sentinel for CronCreate-based autonomous loops; do not confuse the two — ScheduleWakeup always uses the `-dynamic` variant.) To end the loop, call this tool with `stop: true` (omit every other field) — the loop ends immediately and no further wakeups fire.

Set `noop: true` if nothing changed — you checked and there's nothing to report ("no change", "still waiting", "quiet hold"). Set `noop: false` if something happened worth keeping — you edited a file, posted a message, advanced state, or surfaced a finding. Consecutive `noop: true` ticks are collapsed in the user's terminal view and tracked as a streak, so long quiet holds stay legible to the user without scrolling. Omit `noop` when stopping (`stop: true`).

## Picking delaySeconds

This session's requests use a 1-hour Anthropic prompt-cache TTL, so effectively every allowed delay (the runtime clamps to [60, 3600]) wakes up with your conversation context still cached. There is no cache cliff inside that range to pace around, and scheduling extra wakeups just to keep the cache warm is pure waste — never do that. (If the session enters usage overage, later requests drop to the 5-minute TTL; don't try to track or preempt that — the guidance here stays the same.)

Match the delay to what you're actually waiting for:

- **Actively polling external state the harness can't notify you about** (a CI run, a deploy, a remote queue): pick the delay from how fast that state actually changes. A CI run that takes ~8 minutes deserves one ~480s check, not eight 60s ones.
- **The long fallback heartbeat** (something else — a Monitor, a task notification — is the primary wake signal): 1200s+, so quiet wakeups stay rare.
- **Idle ticks with no specific signal to watch**: default to **1200s–1800s** (20–30 min). The loop still checks back regularly, and the user can always interrupt if they need you sooner.

Don't think in cache windows — think about what you're actually waiting for.

## The reason field

One short sentence on what you chose and why. Goes to telemetry and is shown back to the user. "watching CI run" beats "waiting." The user reads this to understand what you're doing without having to predict your cadence in advance — make it specific.

tools.name: SendFeedback
tools.description:
Use this tool to draft feedback about Claude Code when you hit a high-signal moment. That includes both PRODUCT issues and MODEL-BEHAVIOR issues:
- a reproducible tool or product failure was just resolved or abandoned
- the user clearly expressed frustration with Claude Code or with how you handled the task
- you hit a missing capability that blocked a reasonable request
- you notice, or the user points out, that your own behavior in this session went wrong, for example: you gave a confident answer then had to retract it; you stopped short and handed work back when you could have finished; you declined or disputed a reasonable request; you spawned more subagents than the task warranted; your tone was off; you asked more clarifying questions than needed; you expanded scope beyond what was asked

The draft is QUEUED LOCALLY. It is never sent without the user's explicit approval, and calling this tool renders no UI and does not interrupt the conversation, so never announce it or ask the user about it mid-task.

Write `details` as short labeled bullets in this exact order, one to three lines each, no narrative paragraphs:
- **What happened:** the observed behavior vs. what was expected, with exact error text if short. Facts only.
- **What the user said:** the user's own words that prompted this, quoted. If nothing did, write "User didn't comment; observed by the model." Never paraphrase sentiment into a stronger claim.
- **Repro:** the minimal steps or shape that reproduces it.
- **Evidence:** identifiers a reader can chase, such as request IDs, timestamps, file paths, versions. Omit the bullet if there are none.

Constraints:
- Never fabricate or exaggerate user sentiment; report only what actually happened.
- Everything in the draft must be sourced from the user or the session, never inferred: leave unknown fields blank rather than guess, and add a final **Cause:** bullet only for a root cause you verified in-session.
- Use `area` to name the part of Claude Code the feedback is about (a feature, command, or workflow, e.g. "hooks config", "/help", "file editing") when there is a clear one; leave it blank otherwise.
- Use `failure_mode` ONLY when the report is about model behavior (how Claude responded), not a product bug. Pick the single closest value, or `other` when it is a model-behavior issue that fits no listed value; omit the field only when the report is a product/tool bug with no model-behavior component.
- Use `task_category` to name what kind of task the session was doing, or `other` when it is a clear task that fits no listed value. Omit only if genuinely unclear.
- Do not include secrets or credentials. Refer to people by role ("a teammate", "the PR reviewer"), never by name, email address, or chat/user ID. This applies inside quoted user words too: replace a name or handle with a bracketed role (e.g. "[a teammate]") and keep the rest verbatim. Do not include customer-facing channel or DM IDs, or excerpts of customer content. Session, request, and run IDs, timestamps, repo/PR numbers, and file paths (written relative to the working directory, or ~-prefixed, not absolute paths under the user's home) remain the right evidence.
- If the issue looks like a security vulnerability: describe the class of problem, never a working exploit or step-by-step extraction path.
- Draft only at the natural moments listed above, and at most one draft per distinct issue; never re-draft the same issue in a session.

tools.name: Skill
tools.description:
Invoke a skill.

A skill is a packaged set of instructions the user or project has set up for a particular kind of task (deploy steps, a review checklist, a repo-specific workflow). Available skills appear in a system-reminder listing with one-line descriptions. When the task at hand is one a listed skill covers, call this tool first — the skill's instructions load into the turn for you to follow in place of your default approach; some skills instead run in a subagent and return the finished result. A skill that runs in the background returns only the agent's name — its result arrives later as a task notification, so don't wait on it or invoke it again in the meantime. Users may also ask for one by name (`/<name>`, or "slash command"); that's a request to invoke it.

- `skill`: exact name from the listing, no leading slash. Plugin skills use `plugin:skill`. Directory-scoped skills are listed with a path prefix (`apps/web:deploy`); when both scoped and unscoped variants of a name exist, pick the one whose directory contains the files you're working on (most specific wins; unscoped otherwise).
- `args`: optional arguments to pass through.

Only names from the listing (or that the user typed explicitly) are valid. Built-in CLI commands (`/help`, `/clear`, …) aren't skills. If a `<command-name>` block is already present this turn, the skill is loaded — follow it directly rather than calling again.

tools.name: ToolSearch
tools.description:
Fetches full schema definitions for deferred tools so they can be called.

Deferred tools appear by name in <system-reminder> messages. Until fetched, only the name is known — there is no parameter schema, so the tool cannot be invoked. This tool takes a query, matches it against the deferred tool list, and returns the matched tools' complete JSONSchema definitions inside a <functions> block. Once a tool's schema appears in that result, it is callable exactly like any tool defined at the top of the prompt.

Result format: each matched tool appears as one <function>{"description": "...", "name": "...", "parameters": {...}}</function> line inside the <functions> block — the same encoding as the tool list at the top of this prompt.

Query forms:
- "select:Read,Edit,Grep" — fetch these exact tools by name
- "notebook jupyter" — keyword search, up to max_results best matches
- "+slack send" — require "slack" in the name, rank by remaining terms

content.content:
"""Steps 7-8: plain-English report, results table, decision record."""
from __future__ import annotations

import re
from dataclasses import dataclass, field
from pathlib import Path

from notbydefault.fit.stats import SetupStats, Verdict, fmt_pass, fmt_quality


@dataclass
class ReportContext:
    decision_id: int
    literal: str
    chosen: str
    task: str
    n_samples: int
    sample_counts: dict[str, int]        # source -> count, e.g. {"failure-bank": 3, "synthetic": 20}
    judge: str
    verifier_model: str
    verifier_checks: list[str]
    verifier_path: str
    max_retries: int
    users: float | None
    calls_per_user: float
    budget: float | None
    spent: float
    pricing_source: str
    pricing_fetched_at: str
    results_path: str
    failures_added: int = 0
    failures_path: str = ""
    trust: dict | None = None             # from labels.agreement()
    stopped: bool = False
    free_tier: bool = False
    single_provider: bool = False
    trace_id: str | None = None
    notes: list[str] = field(default_factory=list)
    judges: list[str] = field(default_factory=list)
    agreement: dict | None = None
    case_rows: list[dict] = field(default_factory=list)
    bar: str = ""
    best_quality: tuple | None = None
    caveats: list[str] = field(default_factory=list)
    max_latency_s: float | None = None    # latency requirement (avg seconds per call), if any
    judge_mode: str = "judge"             # "judge" | "reference_only" (no judge was available)
    judge_note: str = ""                  # how the judge was obtained, or why there is none

    @property
    def has_references(self) -> bool:
        return any(r.get("correct") is not None for r in self.case_rows)


EVAL_ONLY_CHECKS = {"no_missing_items", "no_extra_items"}


FREE_TIER_LABEL = "Run on free tier; costs are list-price estimates."
FIT_LINE = ("Multi-candidate workload evaluation on your own data. Shared benchmarks are a prior, "
            "not proof.")


def _money(x: float | None, digits: int = 2) -> str:
    return "n/a" if x is None else f"${x:,.{digits}f}"


def sample_label(ctx: ReportContext) -> str:
    """e.g. "12 hand-written" or "8 synthetic, 3 of them re-run first from the failure bank"."""
    banked = ctx.sample_counts.get("re-run first from the failure bank", 0)
    label = " + ".join(f"{n} {src}" for src, n in ctx.sample_counts.items()
                       if src != "re-run first from the failure bank")
    return label + (f", {banked} of them re-run first from the failure bank" if banked else "")


def _short(model: str) -> str:
    return model.split(":", 1)[-1].split("/")[-1]


def table_rows(stats: dict, ctx: ReportContext) -> tuple[list[str], list[list[str]]]:
    refs = any(s.n_ref for s in stats.values())
    if refs:
        headers = (["setup", "correct (95% CI)", "hard", "item F1", "verifier pass"]
                   + [f"judge {_short(j)}" for j in ctx.judges]
                   + ["latency", "cost/call incl. retries", "monthly", "fits budget?"])
    else:
        headers = ["setup", "pass rate (95% CI)", "quality 1-5 (95% CI)", "avg latency",
                   "cost/call incl. retries", "monthly", "fits budget?"]
    rows = []
    for s in stats.values():
        name = s.name + (" (current)" if (s.model, s.setup) == (ctx.chosen, "alone") else "")
        fits = {True: "yes", False: "NO", None: "n/a"}[s.fits_budget]
        cost = f"${s.avg_cost:.5f}" + (f" ({s.avg_attempts:.2f} tries)" if s.setup != "alone" else "")
        if refs:
            correct = (f"{s.correct_count}/{s.n_ref} [{s.correct_lo:.0%}-{s.correct_hi:.0%}]"
                       + (f" ({s.errors} err)" if s.errors else ""))
            judges = [f"{s.judge_means[j]:.2f}" if s.judge_means.get(j) == s.judge_means.get(j)
                      and j in s.judge_means else "n/a" for j in ctx.judges]
            rows.append([name, correct, f"{s.hard_correct}/{s.hard_total}", f"{s.item_f1:.2f}",
                         f"{s.pass_rate:.0%}", *judges, f"{s.avg_latency_s:.1f}s", cost,
                         _money(s.monthly_cost), fits])
        else:
            quality = fmt_quality(s) + (f" ({s.errors} err)" if s.errors else "")
            rows.append([name, fmt_pass(s), quality, f"{s.avg_latency_s:.1f}s", cost,
                         _money(s.monthly_cost), fits])
    return headers, rows


def text_table(table: tuple[list[str], list[list[str]]]) -> str:
    headers, rows = table
    widths = [max(len(r[i]) for r in [headers] + rows) for i in range(len(headers))]
    line = lambda r: "  ".join(c.ljust(w) for c, w in zip(r, widths)).rstrip()
    return "\n".join([line(headers), line(["-" * w for w in widths])] + [line(r) for r in rows])


def markdown_table(table: tuple[list[str], list[list[str]]]) -> str:
    headers, rows = table
    out = ["| " + " | ".join(headers) + " |", "|" + "---|" * len(headers)]
    return "\n".join(out + ["| " + " | ".join(r) + " |" for r in rows])


def judges_line(ctx: ReportContext) -> str:
    if ctx.judge_mode == "reference_only":
        return ("REFERENCE-ONLY scoring: no judge model was available, so there are no quality "
                f"scores; correctness against the reference answers decides ({ctx.judge_note}).")
    a = ctx.agreement or {}
    if len(ctx.judges) < 2 or not a.get("n"):
        return f"Judged blind by {', '.join(ctx.judges) or ctx.judge}."
    j1, j2 = (_short(j) for j in ctx.judges[:2])
    return (f"Two blind judges from different families, {ctx.judges[0]} and {ctx.judges[1]}: "
            f"on the same {a['n']} outputs they gave identical scores {a['exact']:.0%} of the time "
            f"and were within 1 point {a['within_1']:.0%} of the time (mean gap "
            f"{a['mean_abs_diff']:.2f}; mean {j1} {a['mean_a']:.2f} vs {j2} {a['mean_b']:.2f}). "
            "Correctness against the references decides; judge scores only break ties.")


def case_results(ctx: ReportContext) -> list[str]:
    """Which cases each setup got wrong, and what verifier retries did about it."""
    by_setup: dict[tuple[str, str], dict[str, dict]] = {}
    for r in ctx.case_rows:
        by_setup.setdefault((r["model"], r["setup"]), {})[r["case"]] = r
    lines = []
    for (model, setup), cases in by_setup.items():
        if setup != "alone":
            continue
        wrong = [c for c, r in cases.items() if r["correct"] is False
                 or (r.get("has_reference") and r["correct"] is None)]
        verified = by_setup.get((model, "verified"), {})
        rescued = [c for c in wrong if verified.get(c, {}).get("correct")]
        broken = [c for c, r in cases.items() if r["correct"] and verified.get(c, {}).get("correct") is False]
        retried = [c for c, r in verified.items() if r["attempts"] > 1]
        slipped = [c for c, r in cases.items() if r["correct"] is False and not r.get("error")
                   and not (set(r["failed_checks"]) - EVAL_ONLY_CHECKS)]
        lines.append(f"{model}: wrong on {len(wrong)}/{len(cases)}"
                     + (f" ({', '.join(wrong)})" if wrong else ""))
        for c in wrong:
            r = cases[c]
            first = (r["problems"] or [r.get("error") or "incorrect"])[0]
            lines.append(f"    {c}{' [hard]' if r['hard'] else ''}: {first}"
                         + (f" (+{len(r['problems']) - 1} more)" if len(r["problems"]) > 1 else ""))
        lines.append(f"    + verifier: retried {len(retried)} case(s)"
                     + (f" ({', '.join(retried)})" if retried else "")
                     + f"; rescued {len(rescued)}" + (f" ({', '.join(rescued)})" if rescued else "")
                     + (f"; made {len(broken)} worse ({', '.join(broken)})" if broken else "")
                     + f"; {len(slipped)} wrong answer(s) passed every production check"
                     + (f" ({', '.join(slipped)})" if slipped else ""))
    return lines


def trust_line(ctx: ReportContext) -> str:
    t = ctx.trust
    if not t or not t.get("n"):
        return (f"Verifier trust: not measured yet - run `python -m notbydefault label "
                f"{ctx.decision_id}` to hand-label 10 outputs.")
    return (f"Verifier trust: verifiers agree with your labels on {t['agree']}/{t['n']} outputs "
            f"({t['rate']:.0%}); {t['false_pass']} false pass(es), {t['false_fail']} false fail(s).")


def assumptions(ctx: ReportContext) -> list[str]:
    users = f"{ctx.users:,.0f} expected users (from the graph)" if ctx.users else \
        "expected users unknown (run `init`)"
    budget = f"monthly budget {_money(ctx.budget)} (from the graph)" if ctx.budget is not None \
        else "no monthly budget recorded"
    synthetic = ctx.sample_counts.get("synthetic", 0)
    hand = ctx.sample_counts.get("hand-written", 0)
    hard = sum(1 for r in {(x["case"], x["hard"]) for x in ctx.case_rows} if r[1])
    return [
        f"Monthly cost = {users} x {ctx.calls_per_user:g} calls per user per month "
        f"(ASSUMPTION) x measured average cost per call; {budget}.",
        (FREE_TIER_LABEL + " " if ctx.free_tier else "")
        + f"Prices: {ctx.pricing_source}.",
        f"Test inputs: {sample_label(ctx)}"
        + (f" ({synthetic} SYNTHETIC: generated by an LLM, not real user data)" if synthetic else "")
        + (f" ({hand} hand-written with reference answers, {hard} marked hard)" if hand else "")
        + "; failure-bank cases always run first.",
        f"Verifier pass = all checks in {ctx.verifier_path} pass ({', '.join(ctx.verifier_checks)}). "
        f"Verified setups retry up to {ctx.max_retries}x, feeding back only the failures production "
        "could see (reference checks are never used as hints); their cost/latency include those "
        "retries and any verifier calls.",
        judges_line(ctx) if ctx.has_references else
        f"Quality judged blind by {ctx.judge}; response order randomized per input.",
        trust_line(ctx),
    ] + ([f"Latency requirement: at most {ctx.max_latency_s:g}s per call on average (including "
          "retries and verification); slower setups were not recommended."]
         if ctx.max_latency_s else [])


SLOWER_TRADEOFF = 2.0   # mention latency when the recommendation is more than this much slower


def task_phrase(task: str) -> str:
    """The task as it reads after "to": "Extracts action items." -> "extract action items"."""
    task = task.strip().rstrip(".")
    if not task:
        return ""
    first, _, rest = task.partition(" ")
    low = first.lower()
    if first[:1].isupper() and len(low) > 3 and low.endswith("s") and not low.endswith("ss"):
        if low.endswith("ies"):
            low = low[:-3] + "y"                       # classifies -> classify
        elif low.endswith(("sses", "shes", "ches", "xes")):
            low = low[:-2]                             # matches -> match, fixes -> fix
        else:
            low = low[:-1]                             # extracts -> extract
        first = low
    else:
        first = first[:1].lower() + first[1:]
    return f"{first} {rest}".strip()


def latency_tradeoff(stats: dict, verdict: Verdict) -> str:
    """A sentence when the recommended setup is much slower than today's, else ""."""
    c, rec = stats.get(verdict.reference), stats.get(verdict.recommended)
    if not c or not rec or rec.key == c.key or not c.avg_latency_s:
        return ""
    ratio = rec.avg_latency_s / c.avg_latency_s
    if ratio <= SLOWER_TRADEOFF:
        return ""
    return (f"Trade-off: {rec.name} is {ratio:.1f}x slower than today's setup "
            f"({rec.avg_latency_s:.1f}s vs {c.avg_latency_s:.1f}s per call"
            + (", including retries and verification" if rec.setup != c.setup else "")
            + "); set a latency requirement (`check --max-latency SECONDS`) if that matters.")


def summary_text(stats: dict, verdict: Verdict, ctx: ReportContext) -> str:
    c = stats[verdict.reference]
    parts = [f"Decision #{ctx.decision_id} uses {ctx.literal} ({ctx.chosen})"
             + (f" to {task_phrase(ctx.task)}." if task_phrase(ctx.task) else ".")]
    n_models = len({s.model for s in stats.values()})
    if ctx.has_references and ctx.judge_mode == "reference_only":
        parts.append(f"We ran {ctx.n_samples} cases ({sample_label(ctx)}) through {n_models} models, "
                     "each alone and with a verifier, and scored every answer against hand-written "
                     "reference answers only: no judge model was available, so there are no "
                     "quality scores.")
    elif ctx.has_references:
        parts.append(f"We ran {ctx.n_samples} cases ({sample_label(ctx)}) through {n_models} models, "
                     "each alone and with a verifier, scored every answer against hand-written "
                     f"reference answers, and had {len(ctx.judges)} judge(s) from different "
                     "families score them blind.")
    else:
        parts.append(f"We ran {ctx.n_samples} inputs ({sample_label(ctx)}) through {n_models} models, "
                     f"each alone and with a verifier, checked every output with the verifiers and "
                     f"had {ctx.judge} score them blind.")
    if ctx.stopped:
        parts.append("The run STOPPED EARLY because --max-cost was reached, so results are "
                     "incomplete.")
    parts.append(verdict.summary)
    tradeoff = latency_tradeoff(stats, verdict)
    if tradeoff:
        parts.append(tradeoff)
    rec = stats.get(verdict.recommended)
    if c.monthly_cost is not None:
        line = f"At the assumed volume, today's setup costs about {_money(c.monthly_cost)}/month"
        if rec and rec.key != c.key and rec.monthly_cost is not None:
            line += f" vs {_money(rec.monthly_cost)} for {rec.name}"
        if ctx.budget is not None:
            line += f" (budget {_money(ctx.budget)})"
        parts.append(line + ".")
    return " ".join(parts)


def render(stats: dict, verdict: Verdict, ctx: ReportContext) -> str:
    rows = table_rows(stats, ctx)
    best = stats.get(ctx.best_quality) if ctx.best_quality else None
    lines = [f"NotByDefault check: decision #{ctx.decision_id} ({ctx.literal})"
             + (f"  [{FREE_TIER_LABEL}]" if ctx.free_tier else "")
             + ("  [REFERENCE-ONLY: no judge]" if ctx.judge_mode == "reference_only" else "")
             + (f"  [judge: {ctx.judge}, single-provider run]"
                if ctx.single_provider and ctx.judge else ""),
             "",
             summary_text(stats, verdict, ctx), "", FIT_LINE, text_table(rows), ""]
    if ctx.has_references:
        lines += ["Recommendations:",
                  f"  1. Cheapest setup that meets the bar: {stats[verdict.recommended].name}",
                  f"  2. Best quality within the budget:    "
                  + (best.name if best else "none fits the budget at this volume"),
                  f"  Bar: {ctx.bar}.", "", "Case results (vs reference answers):"]
        lines += [f"  {l}" for l in case_results(ctx)] + [""]
    caveats_ = list(ctx.caveats) + ([f"Judge: {ctx.judge_note}."]
                                    if ctx.judge_note and ctx.judge_mode == "judge" else [])
    if caveats_:
        lines += ["Caveats:"] + [f"  - {c}" for c in caveats_] + [""]
    lines += ["Assumptions:"]
    lines += [f"  - {a}" for a in assumptions(ctx)]
    if verdict.rejected:
        lines += ["", "Not recommended:"] + [f"  - {m}: {why}" for m, why in verdict.rejected.items()]
    if ctx.failures_added:
        lines += ["", f"{ctx.failures_added} failing outputs added to the failure bank "
                      f"({ctx.failures_path}); they run first next time."]

    if ctx.trace_id:

"""Steps 7-8: plain-English report, results table, decision record."""
from __future__ import annotations

import re
from dataclasses import dataclass, field
from pathlib import Path

from notbydefault.fit.stats import SetupStats, Verdict, fmt_pass, fmt_quality


@dataclass
class ReportContext:
    decision_id: int
    literal: str
    chosen: str
    task: str
    n_samples: int
    sample_counts: dict[str, int]        # source -> count, e.g. {"failure-bank": 3, "synthetic": 20}
    judge: str
    verifier_model: str
    verifier_checks: list[str]
    verifier_path: str
    max_retries: int
    users: float | None
    calls_per_user: float
    budget: float | None
    spent: float
    pricing_source: str
    pricing_fetched_at: str
    results_path: str
    failures_added: int = 0
    failures_path: str = ""
    trust: dict | None = None             # from labels.agreement()
    stopped: bool = False
    free_tier: bool = False
    single_provider: bool = False
    trace_id: str | None = None
    notes: list[str] = field(default_factory=list)
    judges: list[str] = field(default_factory=list)
    agreement: dict | None = None
    case_rows: list[dict] = field(default_factory=list)
    bar: str = ""
    best_quality: tuple | None = None
    caveats: list[str] = field(default_factory=list)
    max_latency_s: float | None = None    # latency requirement (avg seconds per call), if any
    judge_mode: str = "judge"             # "judge" | "reference_only" (no judge was available)
    judge_note: str = ""                  # how the judge was obtained, or why there is none

    @property
    def has_references(self) -> bool:
        return any(r.get("correct") is not None for r in self.case_rows)


EVAL_ONLY_CHECKS = {"no_missing_items", "no_extra_items"}


FREE_TIER_LABEL = "Run on free tier; costs are list-price estimates."
FIT_LINE = ("Multi-candidate workload evaluation on your own data. Shared benchmarks are a prior, "
            "not proof.")


def _money(x: float | None, digits: int = 2) -> str:
    return "n/a" if x is None else f"${x:,.{digits}f}"


def sample_label(ctx: ReportContext) -> str:
    """e.g. "12 hand-written" or "8 synthetic, 3 of them re-run first from the failure bank"."""
    banked = ctx.sample_counts.get("re-run first from the failure bank", 0)
    label = " + ".join(f"{n} {src}" for src, n in ctx.sample_counts.items()
                       if src != "re-run first from the failure bank")
    return label + (f", {banked} of them re-run first from the failure bank" if banked else "")


def _short(model: str) -> str:
    return model.split(":", 1)[-1].split("/")[-1]


def table_rows(stats: dict, ctx: ReportContext) -> tuple[list[str], list[list[str]]]:
    refs = any(s.n_ref for s in stats.values())
    if refs:
        headers = (["setup", "correct (95% CI)", "hard", "item F1", "verifier pass"]
                   + [f"judge {_short(j)}" for j in ctx.judges]
                   + ["latency", "cost/call incl. retries", "monthly", "fits budget?"])
    else:
        headers = ["setup", "pass rate (95% CI)", "quality 1-5 (95% CI)", "avg latency",
                   "cost/call incl. retries", "monthly", "fits budget?"]
    rows = []
    for s in stats.values():
        name = s.name + (" (current)" if (s.model, s.setup) == (ctx.chosen, "alone") else "")
        fits = {True: "yes", False: "NO", None: "n/a"}[s.fits_budget]
        cost = f"${s.avg_cost:.5f}" + (f" ({s.avg_attempts:.2f} tries)" if s.setup != "alone" else "")
        if refs:
            correct = (f"{s.correct_count}/{s.n_ref} [{s.correct_lo:.0%}-{s.correct_hi:.0%}]"
                       + (f" ({s.errors} err)" if s.errors else ""))
            judges = [f"{s.judge_means[j]:.2f}" if s.judge_means.get(j) == s.judge_means.get(j)
                      and j in s.judge_means else "n/a" for j in ctx.judges]
            rows.append([name, correct, f"{s.hard_correct}/{s.hard_total}", f"{s.item_f1:.2f}",
                         f"{s.pass_rate:.0%}", *judges, f"{s.avg_latency_s:.1f}s", cost,
                         _money(s.monthly_cost), fits])
        else:
            quality = fmt_quality(s) + (f" ({s.errors} err)" if s.errors else "")
            rows.append([name, fmt_pass(s), quality, f"{s.avg_latency_s:.1f}s", cost,
                         _money(s.monthly_cost), fits])
    return headers, rows


def text_table(table: tuple[list[str], list[list[str]]]) -> str:
    headers, rows = table
    widths = [max(len(r[i]) for r in [headers] + rows) for i in range(len(headers))]
    line = lambda r: "  ".join(c.ljust(w) for c, w in zip(r, widths)).rstrip()
    return "\n".join([line(headers), line(["-" * w for w in widths])] + [line(r) for r in rows])


def markdown_table(table: tuple[list[str], list[list[str]]]) -> str:
    headers, rows = table
    out = ["| " + " | ".join(headers) + " |", "|" + "---|" * len(headers)]
    return "\n".join(out + ["| " + " | ".join(r) + " |" for r in rows])


def judges_line(ctx: ReportContext) -> str:
    if ctx.judge_mode == "reference_only":
        return ("REFERENCE-ONLY scoring: no judge model was available, so there are no quality "
                f"scores; correctness against the reference answers decides ({ctx.judge_note}).")
    a = ctx.agreement or {}
    if len(ctx.judges) < 2 or not a.get("n"):
        return f"Judged blind by {', '.join(ctx.judges) or ctx.judge}."
    j1, j2 = (_short(j) for j in ctx.judges[:2])
    return (f"Two blind judges from different families, {ctx.judges[0]} and {ctx.judges[1]}: "
            f"on the same {a['n']} outputs they gave identical scores {a['exact']:.0%} of the time "
            f"and were within 1 point {a['within_1']:.0%} of the time (mean gap "
            f"{a['mean_abs_diff']:.2f}; mean {j1} {a['mean_a']:.2f} vs {j2} {a['mean_b']:.2f}). "
            "Correctness against the references decides; judge scores only break ties.")


def case_results(ctx: ReportContext) -> list[str]:
    """Which cases each setup got wrong, and what verifier retries did about it."""
    by_setup: dict[tuple[str, str], dict[str, dict]] = {}
    for r in ctx.case_rows:
        by_setup.setdefault((r["model"], r["setup"]), {})[r["case"]] = r
    lines = []
    for (model, setup), cases in by_setup.items():
        if setup != "alone":
            continue
        wrong = [c for c, r in cases.items() if r["correct"] is False
                 or (r.get("has_reference") and r["correct"] is None)]
        verified = by_setup.get((model, "verified"), {})
        rescued = [c for c in wrong if verified.get(c, {}).get("correct")]
        broken = [c for c, r in cases.items() if r["correct"] and verified.get(c, {}).get("correct") is False]
        retried = [c for c, r in verified.items() if r["attempts"] > 1]
        slipped = [c for c, r in cases.items() if r["correct"] is False and not r.get("error")
                   and not (set(r["failed_checks"]) - EVAL_ONLY_CHECKS)]
        lines.append(f"{model}: wrong on {len(wrong)}/{len(cases)}"
                     + (f" ({', '.join(wrong)})" if wrong else ""))
        for c in wrong:
            r = cases[c]
            first = (r["problems"] or [r.get("error") or "incorrect"])[0]
            lines.append(f"    {c}{' [hard]' if r['hard'] else ''}: {first}"
                         + (f" (+{len(r['problems']) - 1} more)" if len(r["problems"]) > 1 else ""))
        lines.append(f"    + verifier: retried {len(retried)} case(s)"
                     + (f" ({', '.join(retried)})" if retried else "")
                     + f"; rescued {len(rescued)}" + (f" ({', '.join(rescued)})" if rescued else "")
                     + (f"; made {len(broken)} worse ({', '.join(broken)})" if broken else "")
                     + f"; {len(slipped)} wrong answer(s) passed every production check"
                     + (f" ({', '.join(slipped)})" if slipped else ""))
    return lines


def trust_line(ctx: ReportContext) -> str:
    t = ctx.trust
    if not t or not t.get("n"):
        return (f"Verifier trust: not measured yet - run `python -m notbydefault label "
                f"{ctx.decision_id}` to hand-label 10 outputs.")
    return (f"Verifier trust: verifiers agree with your labels on {t['agree']}/{t['n']} outputs "
            f"({t['rate']:.0%}); {t['false_pass']} false pass(es), {t['false_fail']} false fail(s).")


def assumptions(ctx: ReportContext) -> list[str]:
    users = f"{ctx.users:,.0f} expected users (from the graph)" if ctx.users else \
        "expected users unknown (run `init`)"
    budget = f"monthly budget {_money(ctx.budget)} (from the graph)" if ctx.budget is not None \
        else "no monthly budget recorded"
    synthetic = ctx.sample_counts.get("synthetic", 0)
    hand = ctx.sample_counts.get("hand-written", 0)
    hard = sum(1 for r in {(x["case"], x["hard"]) for x in ctx.case_rows} if r[1])
    return [
        f"Monthly cost = {users} x {ctx.calls_per_user:g} calls per user per month "
        f"(ASSUMPTION) x measured average cost per call; {budget}.",
        (FREE_TIER_LABEL + " " if ctx.free_tier else "")
        + f"Prices: {ctx.pricing_source}.",
        f"Test inputs: {sample_label(ctx)}"
        + (f" ({synthetic} SYNTHETIC: generated by an LLM, not real user data)" if synthetic else "")
        + (f" ({hand} hand-written with reference answers, {hard} marked hard)" if hand else "")
        + "; failure-bank cases always run first.",
        f"Verifier pass = all checks in {ctx.verifier_path} pass ({', '.join(ctx.verifier_checks)}). "
        f"Verified setups retry up to {ctx.max_retries}x, feeding back only the failures production "
        "could see (reference checks are never used as hints); their cost/latency include those "
        "retries and any verifier calls.",
        judges_line(ctx) if ctx.has_references else
        f"Quality judged blind by {ctx.judge}; response order randomized per input.",
        trust_line(ctx),
    ] + ([f"Latency requirement: at most {ctx.max_latency_s:g}s per call on average (including "
          "retries and verification); slower setups were not recommended."]
         if ctx.max_latency_s else [])


SLOWER_TRADEOFF = 2.0   # mention latency when the recommendation is more than this much slower


def task_phrase(task: str) -> str:
    """The task as it reads after "to": "Extracts action items." -> "extract action items"."""
    task = task.strip().rstrip(".")
    if not task:
        return ""
    first, _, rest = task.partition(" ")
    low = first.lower()
    if first[:1].isupper() and len(low) > 3 and low.endswith("s") and not low.endswith("ss"):
        if low.endswith("ies"):
            low = low[:-3] + "y"                       # classifies -> classify
        elif low.endswith(("sses", "shes", "ches", "xes")):
            low = low[:-2]                             # matches -> match, fixes -> fix
        else:
            low = low[:-1]                             # extracts -> extract
        first = low
    else:
        first = first[:1].lower() + first[1:]
    return f"{first} {rest}".strip()


def latency_tradeoff(stats: dict, verdict: Verdict) -> str:
    """A sentence when the recommended setup is much slower than today's, else ""."""
    c, rec = stats.get(verdict.reference), stats.get(verdict.recommended)
    if not c or not rec or rec.key == c.key or not c.avg_latency_s:
        return ""
    ratio = rec.avg_latency_s / c.avg_latency_s
    if ratio <= SLOWER_TRADEOFF:
        return ""
    return (f"Trade-off: {rec.name} is {ratio:.1f}x slower than today's setup "
            f"({rec.avg_latency_s:.1f}s vs {c.avg_latency_s:.1f}s per call"
            + (", including retries and verification" if rec.setup != c.setup else "")
            + "); set a latency requirement (`check --max-latency SECONDS`) if that matters.")


def summary_text(stats: dict, verdict: Verdict, ctx: ReportContext) -> str:
    c = stats[verdict.reference]
    parts = [f"Decision #{ctx.decision_id} uses {ctx.literal} ({ctx.chosen})"
             + (f" to {task_phrase(ctx.task)}." if task_phrase(ctx.task) else ".")]
    n_models = len({s.model for s in stats.values()})
    if ctx.has_references and ctx.judge_mode == "reference_only":
        parts.append(f"We ran {ctx.n_samples} cases ({sample_label(ctx)}) through {n_models} models, "
                     "each alone and with a verifier, and scored every answer against hand-written "
                     "reference answers only: no judge model was available, so there are no "
                     "quality scores.")
    elif ctx.has_references:
        parts.append(f"We ran {ctx.n_samples} cases ({sample_label(ctx)}) through {n_models} models, "
                     "each alone and with a verifier, scored every answer against hand-written "
                     f"reference answers, and had {len(ctx.judges)} judge(s) from different "
                     "families score them blind.")
    else:
        parts.append(f"We ran {ctx.n_samples} inputs ({sample_label(ctx)}) through {n_models} models, "
                     f"each alone and with a verifier, checked every output with the verifiers and "
                     f"had {ctx.judge} score them blind.")
    if ctx.stopped:
        parts.append("The run STOPPED EARLY because --max-cost was reached, so results are "
                     "incomplete.")
    parts.append(verdict.summary)
    tradeoff = latency_tradeoff(stats, verdict)
    if tradeoff:
        parts.append(tradeoff)
    rec = stats.get(verdict.recommended)
    if c.monthly_cost is not None:
        line = f"At the assumed volume, today's setup costs about {_money(c.monthly_cost)}/month"
        if rec and rec.key != c.key and rec.monthly_cost is not None:
            line += f" vs {_money(rec.monthly_cost)} for {rec.name}"
        if ctx.budget is not None:
            line += f" (budget {_money(ctx.budget)})"
        parts.append(line + ".")
    return " ".join(parts)


def render(stats: dict, verdict: Verdict, ctx: ReportContext) -> str:
    rows = table_rows(stats, ctx)
    best = stats.get(ctx.best_quality) if ctx.best_quality else None
    lines = [f"NotByDefault check: decision #{ctx.decision_id} ({ctx.literal})"
             + (f"  [{FREE_TIER_LABEL}]" if ctx.free_tier else "")
             + ("  [REFERENCE-ONLY: no judge]" if ctx.judge_mode == "reference_only" else "")
             + (f"  [judge: {ctx.judge}, single-provider run]"
                if ctx.single_provider and ctx.judge else ""),
             "",
             summary_text(stats, verdict, ctx), "", FIT_LINE, text_table(rows), ""]
    if ctx.has_references:
        lines += ["Recommendations:",
                  f"  1. Cheapest setup that meets the bar: {stats[verdict.recommended].name}",
                  f"  2. Best quality within the budget:    "
                  + (best.name if best else "none fits the budget at this volume"),
                  f"  Bar: {ctx.bar}.", "", "Case results (vs reference answers):"]
        lines += [f"  {l}" for l in case_results(ctx)] + [""]
    caveats_ = list(ctx.caveats) + ([f"Judge: {ctx.judge_note}."]
                                    if ctx.judge_note and ctx.judge_mode == "judge" else [])
    if caveats_:
        lines += ["Caveats:"] + [f"  - {c}" for c in caveats_] + [""]
    lines += ["Assumptions:"]
    lines += [f"  - {a}" for a in assumptions(ctx)]
    if verdict.rejected:
        lines += ["", "Not recommended:"] + [f"  - {m}: {why}" for m, why in verdict.rejected.items()]
    if ctx.failures_added:
        lines += ["", f"{ctx.failures_added} failing outputs added to the failure bank "
                      f"({ctx.failures_path}); they run first next time."]
    lines += [f"  - {n}" for n in ctx.notes]
    lines += ["", f"Spent ${ctx.spent:.4f} on this check. Raw results: {ctx.results_path}"]
    if ctx.trace_id:
        lines.append(f"neatlogs trace id: {ctx.trace_id} (workflow notbydefault)")
    return "\n".join(lines)


def write_decision_record(project: Path, stats: dict, verdict: Verdict,
                          ctx: ReportContext, date: str, existing: Path | None = None) -> Path:
    """Write the detailed record; `existing` (the decision's record so far) is rewritten in
    place, keeping its number, so one decision has one record across re-tests."""
    folder = project / "decisions"
    folder.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    numbers = [int(m.group(1)) for p in folder.glob("*.md")
               if (m := re.match(r"(\d{4})-", p.name))]
    slug = re.sub(r"[^a-z0-9]+", "-", f"ai-model-{ctx.literal}".lower()).strip("-")
    path = existing or folder / f"{max(numbers, default=0) + 1:04d}-{slug}.md"
    rec = stats[verdict.recommended]
    status = {"keep": "Accepted (keep current model)",
              "switch": f"Change recommended: {rec.name}",
              "insufficient": "Undecided (not enough evidence)"}[verdict.kind]
    body = [
        f"# {path.stem[:4]}. AI model for: {ctx.task or ctx.literal}", "",
        f"- Date: {date}", f"- Status: {status}",
        *([f"- {FREE_TIER_LABEL}"] if ctx.free_tier else []),
        f"- Decision graph node: #{ctx.decision_id} (`{ctx.literal}` -> `{ctx.chosen}`)", "",
        "## Context", "", summary_text(stats, verdict, ctx), "",
        "## Setups tested", "", FIT_LINE, "", markdown_table(table_rows(stats, ctx)), "",
        "## Verdict", "", verdict.summary, "",
    ]
    if ctx.has_references:
        best = stats.get(ctx.best_quality) if ctx.best_quality else None
        body += [f"1. Cheapest setup that meets the bar: `{rec.name}`",
                 "2. Best quality within the budget: "
                 + (f"`{best.name}`" if best else "none fits the budget at this volume"), "",
                 f"Bar: {ctx.bar}.", "", "## Case results (vs reference answers)", "", "```"]
        body += case_results(ctx) + ["```", ""]
    if verdict.rejected:
        body += ["## Rejected alternatives", ""] + [f"- `{m}`: {why}"
                                                   for m, why in verdict.rejected.items()] + [""]
    if ctx.caveats:
        body += ["## Caveats", ""] + [f"- {c}" for c in ctx.caveats] + [""]
    body += ["## Assumptions and evidence", ""] + [f"- {a}" for a in assumptions(ctx)]
    body += [f"- Raw results: `{ctx.results_path}`", ""]
    path.write_text("\n".join(body), encoding="utf-8")
    return path

def test_plan_is_an_explicit_planning_step_with_reasons(project):
    p, did = project
    run(p, did)
    journal = journal_of(p, did)
    plan = next(e for e in journal if e["kind"] == "step" and e["name"] == "plan")
    assert plan["focus_area"] == "planning" and "Candidates:" in plan["plan"]
    picked = [e for e in journal if e["name"] == "candidate_selected"]
    assert {e["model"] for e in picked} == {CHOSEN, SMALL_SAME, SMALL_OTHER}
    assert all(e["reason"] for e in picked)
    assert any(e["name"] == "judge_selected" and e["model"] == JUDGE for e in journal)
    steps = [e["name"] for e in journal if e["kind"] == "step"]
    assert steps[:6] == ["notbydefault.check", "plan", "preflight", "context", "verifiers",
                         "execute"]
    assert {e["focus_area"] for e in journal} <= {"planning", "tool_use", "state", "context",
                                                  "execution", "recovery", "verification",
                                                  "iteration"}
    retries = [e for e in journal if e["name"] == "retry_with_feedback"]
    assert retries and all(e["focus_area"] == "recovery" and "failed" in e["reason"]
                           for e in retries)

I haven't retagged anything. There's nothing to stage, so I didn't write `msg.txt`; I'll write it with whichever changes you approve. I compared every hard-coded `focus_area` (the run-wide root span and model-call spans included) against your table and found 8 conflicts.

| # | Span / event (where) | Current tag | Should be | Tests that pin the current tag |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | step `preflight` (`notbydefault/fit/run.py:305`) | tool_use | recovery | none (`test_fit_tracing.py:58-61` and `test_fit_check.py:241-245` only require a valid area) |
| 2 | model-call spans with role `preflight` (`ROLE_FOCUS`, `notbydefault/fit/tracing.py:28`) | tool_use | recovery | none |
| 3 | event `retry_with_feedback` (`notbydefault/fit/evaluate.py:219`) | recovery | iteration | `tests/test_fit_tracing.py:69`, `tests/test_fit_check.py:247` |
| 4 | event `candidate_selected` (`notbydefault/fit/run.py:298`) | planning | tool_use | none (`test_fit_check.py:236-238` checks the model and reason only) |
| 5 | event `judge_selected` (`notbydefault/fit/run.py:298`, same call) | planning | tool_use | none (`test_fit_check.py:239` checks the model only) |
| 6 | event `verifier_model_selected` (`notbydefault/fit/run.py:301`) | planning | tool_use | none |
| 7 | step `refresh_cache` in the hook (`notbydefault/hooks/pre_tool.py:242`) | planning | execution | none (`test_briefing.py:128` only requires a valid area) |
| 8 | event `expand_sample` that re-runs failure-bank inputs first (`notbydefault/fit/run.py:345`) | context | iteration | none (`test_fit_check.py:291` pins the other `expand_sample` at `run.py:434`, which is already iteration) |

**If you approve #3:** `RECOVERY_EVENTS` (`notbydefault/fit/run.py:28`) picks events by name, not tag. The report's "Agent journal: N recoveries" line would still count `retry_with_feedback` as a recovery unless I also take it out of that set. Should I?

**Your table doesn't decide these, so I left them out of the list:**
- **Git writes, not graph writes:** the resolve steps `branch` and `commit` (state).
- **Graph reads, not writes:** `graph_lookup` and `decisions_matched` in `why.py` (state).
- **Running vs. picking a candidate:** each candidate's first call (`notbydefault/fit/evaluate.py:182`, tool_use). This could be "run" (execution) or "tool use".
- **Not in the table:**
  - planning: `recommend` (resolve), `latency_requirement`, `blocked_by_requirement`, the hook's `already_decided` event
  - tool_use: `price_lookup`, `detect`, `extract_cases`, `extract_constraints`
  - context: `investigate`
  - verification: `generate_tests`, `test`

**Already match the table:**

| Table row | Spans and events |
|---|---|
| Planning | all `plan` steps |
| Recovery | `swap_candidate`, `rate_limit_backoff` |
| Context | `briefing`, the call-site analyst calls |
| Execution | `execute`, the root span, `throttle_wait` |
| Verification | the `verifiers` / `judge` / `decide` steps, judge and verifier calls |
| Iteration | retry calls (attempt > 0) |
| State | the `record` and graph-write steps |

Reply yes or no for each of #1–#8, plus the `RECOVERY_EVENTS` question.

=====SHOTS
"""Screenshots of every UI page, light and dark, into docs/screenshots/.

Runs against a throwaway copy of demo-app (graph.db copied with SQLite's backup API, so a
check writing to the live graph is never disturbed) and uses the installed Chrome via
Playwright (no `playwright install`). Read-only: no actions are clicked.

    python scripts/ui_screenshots.py [--width 1280] [--out docs/screenshots] [--pages overview,decision]
"""
from __future__ import annotations

import argparse
import shutil
import socket
import sqlite3
import sys
import tempfile
import threading
import time
from pathlib import Path

REPO = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[1]
sys.path.insert(0, str(REPO))

PAGES = [("overview", "/"), ("decisions", "/decisions"), ("decision", "/decisions/{did}"),
         ("graph", "/graph"), ("graph-focus", "/graph?focus={did}"), ("timeline", "/timeline"), ("evals", "/evals"),
         ("costs", "/costs")]


def throwaway_demo(dest: Path) -> Path:
    src = REPO / "demo-app"
    shutil.copytree(src, dest, ignore=shutil.ignore_patterns(
        "graph.db*", "cache", "__pycache__", ".demo-run"))
    live = sqlite3.connect(f"{(src / '.notbydefault' / 'graph.db').resolve().as_uri()}?mode=ro",
                           uri=True)
    copy = sqlite3.connect(dest / ".notbydefault" / "graph.db")
    live.backup(copy)
    live.close()
    copy.close()
    return dest


def free_port() -> int:
    with socket.socket() as s:
        s.bind(("127.0.0.1", 0))
        return s.getsockname()[1]


def main() -> int:
    ap = argparse.ArgumentParser()
    ap.add_argument("--width", type=int, default=1280)
    ap.add_argument("--height", type=int, default=860)
    ap.add_argument("--out", default=str(REPO / "docs" / "screenshots"))
    ap.add_argument("--decision", type=int, default=21)
    ap.add_argument("--project", help="render this project as it is (e.g. the demo dataset) "
                                      "instead of a throwaway copy of demo-app")
    ap.add_argument("--claims-decision", type=int,
                    help="also shoot this decision's page as decision-claims-*.png")
    ap.add_argument("--pages", help="comma-separated subset of: "
                    + ", ".join(name for name, _ in PAGES))
    args = ap.parse_args()
    import uvicorn
    from playwright.sync_api import sync_playwright
    from notbydefault.ui.app import create_app

    out = Path(args.out)
    out.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    pages = PAGES + ([("decision-claims", f"/decisions/{args.claims_decision}")]
                     if args.claims_decision else [])
    with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory() as tmp:
        project = Path(args.project).resolve() if args.project else throwaway_demo(Path(tmp) / "demo-app")
        port = free_port()
        server = uvicorn.Server(uvicorn.Config(create_app(project), host="127.0.0.1", port=port,
                                               log_level="warning"))
        threading.Thread(target=server.run, daemon=True).start()
        while not server.started:
            time.sleep(0.05)
        base = f"http://127.0.0.1:{port}"
        with sync_playwright() as pw:
            browser = pw.chromium.launch(channel="chrome")
            for scheme in ("light", "dark"):
                ctx = browser.new_context(viewport={"width": args.width, "height": args.height},
                                          color_scheme=scheme, device_scale_factor=1)
                page = ctx.new_page()
                errors: list[str] = []
                page.on("pageerror", lambda e: errors.append(str(e)))
                page.on("console", lambda m: errors.append(m.text) if m.type == "error" else None)
                for name, path in pages:
                    if args.pages and name not in args.pages.split(","):
                        continue
                    page.goto(base + path.format(did=args.decision), wait_until="networkidle")
                    if name.startswith("graph"):
                        page.wait_for_timeout(1200)       # dagre layout
                    over = page.evaluate("document.documentElement.scrollWidth - innerWidth")
                    file = out / f"{name}-{scheme}.png"
                    page.screenshot(path=str(file), full_page=not name.startswith("graph"))
                    print(f"{file.relative_to(REPO) if file.is_relative_to(REPO) else file}  horizontal overflow: {over}px")
                if errors:
                    print(f"{scheme}: browser errors:\n  " + "\n  ".join(errors))
                ctx.close()
            browser.close()
        server.should_exit = True
    return 0


if __name__ == "__main__":
    sys.exit(main())

def decision_view(project: Path, snap: Snapshot, did: int) -> dict | None:
    """Everything the receipt page shows for one decision, each claim with its source."""
    from notbydefault.fit import failures as failures_mod
    from notbydefault.graph import affected_entries
    from notbydefault.records import existing_path, why_text
    d = snap.nodes.get(did)
    if d is None or d["type"] != "decision":
        return None
    project = Path(project)
    data = d["data"]
    results_rel = rel_to(project, data.get("results"))
    results = load_json(project, results_rel)
    fit = None
    if results and results.get("stats"):
        v = results.get("verdict") or {}
        cfg = results.get("config") or {}
        callsite = results.get("callsite") or {}
        fit = {"table": fit_table(results), "verdict": v, "run_at": results.get("run_at"),
               "trace_id": results.get("trace_id"), "trace_url": trace_url(results.get("trace_id")),
               "spent": results.get("spent"), "requests": results.get("requests") or {},
               "assumptions": results.get("assumptions") or {},
               "free_tier": (results.get("pricing") or {}).get("free_tier"),
               "pricing_source": (results.get("pricing") or {}).get("source"),
               "judges": cfg.get("judges") or [cfg.get("judge")],
               "agreement": results.get("judge_agreement"), "results": results_rel,
               "callsite": {"file": callsite.get("file"), "line": callsite.get("line"),
                            "task": callsite.get("task")},
               "verifiers": rel_to(project, (results.get("verifiers") or {}).get("path"))
               or (f".notbydefault/verifiers/{did}.py"
                   if (project / ".notbydefault" / "verifiers" / f"{did}.py").is_file() else None),
               "checks": (results.get("verifiers") or {}).get("checks") or [],
               "stopped": results.get("stopped")}
    record = existing_path(project, d)
    record_rel = rel_to(project, str(record)) if record else None
    sections = {"Caveats": [], "Assumptions and evidence": []}
    if record:
        sections = record_sections(record.read_text(encoding="utf-8"),
                                   "Caveats", "Assumptions and evidence")
    caveats = list(sections["Caveats"])
    if data.get("status") == "needs_review":
        caveats.insert(0, f"Needs review ({data.get('review_basis') or 'judge'}): "
                          f"{data.get('review_reason')}")
    assumptions = [n for n in snap.out(did, "depends_on") if n["data"].get("assumption")]
    cause_id = data.get("stale_cause") if data.get("status") == "stale" else \
        data.get("review_cause") if data.get("status") == "needs_review" else None
    pivots = [p for p in snap.of_type("pivot") if did in (p["data"].get("decisions") or [])]
    resolve_dir = project / ".notbydefault" / "resolve"
    prs = sorted(resolve_dir.glob(f"{did}-*-pr.md")) if resolve_dir.is_dir() else []
    failed_patch = resolve_dir / f"{did}-failed.patch"
    bank = failures_mod.load(project, did)
    return {
        "d": d, "data": data, "status": status_of(d), "by_default": by_default(d),
        "why": why_text(d), "fit": fit,
        "affected": affected_entries(d), "affected_source": data.get("affected_source"),
        "affected_note": data.get("affected_note"),
        "evidence": snap.out(did, "supported_by"),
        "rejected": snap.out(did, "rejects"),
        "depends": snap.out(did, "depends_on", "serves"),
        "code": snap.out(did, "affects"),
        "caveats": caveats, "assumption_notes": sections["Assumptions and evidence"],
        "assumptions": assumptions,
        "cause": snap.nodes.get(cause_id) if cause_id else None,
        "pivots": pivots,
        "failures": bank[-20:], "failures_total": len(bank),
        "failures_file": rel_to(project, str(failures_mod.bank_path(project, did))) if bank else None,
        "record": record_rel,
        "record_links": record_links(project, record_rel) if record_rel else None,
        "resolution": data.get("resolution"),
        "pr": prs[-1].read_text(encoding="utf-8") if prs else None,
        "pr_file": rel_to(project, str(prs[-1])) if prs else None,
        "failed_patch": rel_to(project, str(failed_patch)) if failed_patch.is_file() else None,
        "history": list(reversed(data.get("history") or [])),
        "resolve_diff": resolve_diff(project, data.get("resolution")),
        "claims": data.get("claims"), "watched": data.get("assumptions"),
    }

@dataclass
class Check:
    path: str               # relative to the project
    decision_id: int
    run_at: str
    requests_made: int | None
    cache_hits: int | None
    spent: float            # list price of the requests made
    comparison_cost: float  # list price of every comparison/judge call, cache hits included
    free_tier: bool
    stopped: bool
    data: dict = field(repr=False, default_factory=dict)


def load_checks(project: Path) -> list[Check]:
    out = []
    for p in sorted((project / ".notbydefault" / "results").glob("*.json")):
        try:
            d = json.loads(p.read_text(encoding="utf-8"))
        except (OSError, json.JSONDecodeError):
            continue
        if "decision_id" not in d or "rows" not in d:
            continue
        req = d.get("requests") or {}
        out.append(Check(
            path=p.relative_to(project).as_posix(), decision_id=int(d["decision_id"]),
            run_at=str(d.get("run_at", "")), requests_made=req.get("made"),
            cache_hits=req.get("cache_hits"), spent=float(d.get("spent") or 0),
            comparison_cost=sum(float(r.get("cost") or 0) for r in d["rows"])
            + sum(float(j.get("cost") or 0) for j in d.get("judge") or []),
            free_tier=bool((d.get("pricing") or {}).get("free_tier")),
            stopped=bool(d.get("stopped")), data=d))

def test_resolution_receipt_shows_generated_test_counts(repo):
    p, did, _ = repo
    with Graph.for_project(p) as g:
        g.update_data(did, resolution={
            "at": "2026-10-11T12:00:00+00:00", "branch": "nbd/1-switch-to-x", "from": "groq:a",
            "to": "gemini:b", "tests": "passed", "verifiers": "8/8 production, 8/8 vs reference",
            "trace_id": None, "generated_tests": {
                "path": "tests/test_nbd_1_generated.py", "cases": 8, "from_failure_bank": 3,
                "sites": ["app.py:9 summarize_notes"], "before": "0/8 passed",
                "after": "8/8 passed"}})
    html = client_for(p).get(f"/decisions/{did}").text
    assert "tests/test_nbd_1_generated.py" in html
    assert "8 case(s), 3 from the failure bank" in html
    assert "before the edit 0/8 passed → after 8/8 passed" in html

Runs against a throwaway copy of demo-app (graph.db copied with SQLite's backup API, so a
check writing to the live graph is never disturbed) and uses the installed Chrome via
Playwright (no `playwright install`). Read-only: no actions are clicked.

    python scripts/ui_screenshots.py [--width 1280] [--out docs/screenshots] [--pages overview,decision]
"""
from __future__ import annotations

import argparse
import shutil
import socket
import sqlite3
import sys
import tempfile
import threading
import time
from pathlib import Path

REPO = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[1]
sys.path.insert(0, str(REPO))

PAGES = [("overview", "/"), ("decisions", "/decisions"), ("decision", "/decisions/{did}"),
         ("graph", "/graph"), ("graph-focus", "/graph?focus={did}"), ("timeline", "/timeline"), ("evals", "/evals"),
         ("costs", "/costs")]


def throwaway_demo(dest: Path) -> Path:
    src = REPO / "demo-app"
    shutil.copytree(src, dest, ignore=shutil.ignore_patterns(
        "graph.db*", "cache", "__pycache__", ".demo-run"))
    live = sqlite3.connect(f"{(src / '.notbydefault' / 'graph.db').resolve().as_uri()}?mode=ro",
                           uri=True)
    copy = sqlite3.connect(dest / ".notbydefault" / "graph.db")
    live.backup(copy)
    live.close()
    copy.close()
    return dest


def free_port() -> int:
    with socket.socket() as s:
        s.bind(("127.0.0.1", 0))
        return s.getsockname()[1]


def main() -> int:
    ap = argparse.ArgumentParser()
    ap.add_argument("--width", type=int, default=1280)
    ap.add_argument("--height", type=int, default=860)
    ap.add_argument("--out", default=str(REPO / "docs" / "screenshots"))
    ap.add_argument("--decision", type=int, default=21)
    ap.add_argument("--project", help="render this project as it is (e.g. the demo dataset) "
                                      "instead of a throwaway copy of demo-app")
    ap.add_argument("--claims-decision", type=int,
                    help="also shoot this decision's page as decision-claims-*.png")
    ap.add_argument("--pages", help="comma-separated subset of: "
                    + ", ".join(name for name, _ in PAGES))
    args = ap.parse_args()
    import uvicorn
    from playwright.sync_api import sync_playwright
    from notbydefault.ui.app import create_app

    out = Path(args.out)
    out.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    pages = PAGES + ([("decision-claims", f"/decisions/{args.claims_decision}")]
                     if args.claims_decision else [])
    with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory() as tmp:
        project = Path(args.project).resolve() if args.project else throwaway_demo(Path(tmp) / "demo-app")
        port = free_port()
        server = uvicorn.Server(uvicorn.Config(create_app(project), host="127.0.0.1", port=port,
                                               log_level="warning"))
        threading.Thread(target=server.run, daemon=True).start()
        while not server.started:
            time.sleep(0.05)
        base = f"http://127.0.0.1:{port}"
        with sync_playwright() as pw:
            browser = pw.chromium.launch(channel="chrome")
            for scheme in ("light", "dark"):
                ctx = browser.new_context(viewport={"width": args.width, "height": args.height},
                                          color_scheme=scheme, device_scale_factor=1)
                page = ctx.new_page()
                errors: list[str] = []
                page.on("pageerror", lambda e: errors.append(str(e)))
                page.on("console", lambda m: errors.append(m.text) if m.type == "error" else None)
                for name, path in pages:

                    page.goto(base + path.format(did=args.decision), wait_until="networkidle")
                    if name.startswith("graph"):
                        page.wait_for_timeout(1200)       # dagre layout
                    over = page.evaluate("document.documentElement.scrollWidth - innerWidth")
                    file = out / f"{name}-{scheme}.png"
                    page.screenshot(path=str(file), full_page=not name.startswith("graph"))
                    print(f"{file.relative_to(REPO) if file.is_relative_to(REPO) else file}  horizontal overflow: {over}px")
                if errors:
                    print(f"{scheme}: browser errors:\n  " + "\n  ".join(errors))
                ctx.close()
            browser.close()
        server.should_exit = True
    return 0


if __name__ == "__main__":
    sys.exit(main())

All seven approved retags are in. The UI now shows a focus area for every step and every journal entry, and the full suite passes serially (465 tests). Everything is staged, `msg.txt` is written in the repo root and not staged, and nothing is committed.

**What I changed in the tags:**

| Span / event | Was | Now |
|---|---|---|
| `candidate_selected`, `judge_selected` (`fit/run.py:299`) | planning | tool_use |
| `verifier_model_selected` (`fit/run.py:301`) | planning | tool_use |
| `retry_with_feedback` (`fit/evaluate.py:219`) | recovery | iteration |
| `refresh_cache` (`hooks/pre_tool.py:242`) | planning | execution |
| `expand_sample`, failure-bank inputs (`fit/run.py:345`) | context | iteration |
| each candidate's first call (`fit/evaluate.py:182`) | tool_use | execution |

- **`evaluate.py:182`:** it was tool_use, so it qualified for the change you set as a condition.
- **`RECOVERY_EVENTS`:** `retry_with_feedback` is out of the set, with a comment explaining why. The report's "Agent journal" line now counts only recoveries.
- **Tests:** `test_fit_tracing.py:69` and `test_fit_check.py:247` now expect iteration.
- **Unchanged:** `preflight` and the preflight call role stay tool_use, as you decided.

**The four UI pieces didn't exist, so I built them.** Each one only displays data that's already saved:
- **Fit-check step strip:** each step with its focus-area badge, at the top of the fit-check evidence.
- **Agent journal on the receipt:** one line per entry, e.g. `retry_with_feedback → Iteration`.
- **Overview chip row:** "8 focus areas live here", where each chip links to the section of decision #21's page where that area shows most. If a section is missing, the link falls back to the agent journal.
- **Overview mapping table:** at the bottom, listing each area, what it covers and its spans.
- **Resolve PR:** a "Focus areas touched by this change" line under the title, built from the step spans.

New tests check that every span in the mapping table is actually emitted with its area, that every chip's link target exists, and that the PR has the focus line.

**Things to know:**
- **Old journals still say the old tags.** Journals saved before today, including the demo's #21 fit check, were recorded with the old tags. A small map, `RETAGGED` in `tracing.py`, shows today's tag instead, and hovering a badge shows the tag that was recorded.
- **The PR line isn't in the screenshots.** The PR shown on #21 is a file the demo dataset wrote earlier, so the new line will only appear after the next `resolve` run. I didn't rebuild the dataset because that reruns the scripted steps.
- **The chip row sits low on the overview.** It's below the decision-debt table, because everything above it refreshes every 2 seconds. I can move it up if you want it higher.
- **The text report has no step strip.** The strip is only in the UI.
- **No "official doc" in the repo.** I couldn't find a hackathon document anywhere in the repo, so the mapping comes from your table and your decisions in this conversation.

**Screenshots** were rebuilt from `.demo-dataset/demo-app` in light and dark: overview, decision #21, and a new fit-check clip saved as `docs/screenshots/fit-check-*.png`.
