# NotByDefault

**Prove the choice. Recheck the decision.**

AI coding agents pick models, databases and SDKs by default and give a reason. NotByDefault checks whether that reason is true on your project's own data, records the evidence, and reopens the decision when a requirement, price or fact changes.

> No decision without a why.

## Example

An agent picked `openai/gpt-oss-120b` for an action-items endpoint because it was "cost-effective, strong at extraction, widely used". On the project's 12 cases it scored 10/12 at $407/mo, over the $375 budget. `gemini-3.1-flash-lite` scored 11/12 within budget. `notbydefault resolve 21` switched to it on a branch, with generated tests going from 0/12 to 12/12, and wrote the PR.

When the requirement "data must stay in the EU" was added, that decision was flagged **needs_review** (no documented regional guarantee) and an older Groq decision **stale** (Groq documents US-only). Stale means a known fact breaks it; needs_review means a human should judge.

Trace in neatlogs: `4bcff389ab979638e4ffa7ee88619318`

## How it works

1. **Catch.** A Claude Code `PreToolUse` hook spots a decision when the agent writes a model name, installs an SDK or edits a manifest. It runs in under 300 ms and never blocks the agent.
2. **Record.** The decision, the agent's stated reason and the code it touches go into a decision graph (SQLite, stored with the repo).
3. **Check the reasons.** `claims` splits the reason into cost, quality, latency, compliance and popularity claims, and gives each a verdict with a source. "Widely used" is never evidence for your project.
4. **Check the choice.** `check` runs several candidates on your own cases. Verifiers catch bad outputs, two judges from different model families score them, and confidence intervals flag runs that are too close to call.
5. **Act.** `resolve` applies the winner on a branch (`nbd/<id>-<slug>`), edits only that decision's call sites, generates tests from past failures and writes the PR text. It never touches main or pushes.
6. **Watch.** Each decision stores its assumptions: budget, volume, prices, data region, requirements. `watch` and `require` reopen the affected decisions when any of them change.
7. **Review.** `ui` shows the decision graph, a receipt per decision with its full evidence, a change timeline, eval results and costs. `scan` scores the repo's decision debt (the demo repo scores 14).

## Commands

| Command | What it does |
|---|---|
| `notbydefault check <id>` | Fit-check a decision on your own cases |
| `notbydefault claims <id>` | Verdict on each claim in the agent's reason |
| `notbydefault resolve <id>` | Apply the winner on a branch, with tests and PR text |
| `notbydefault require <project> "<text>"` | Add a requirement; mark decisions stale or needs_review |
| `notbydefault watch` | Reopen decisions whose assumptions changed |
| `notbydefault why "<question>"` | Answer from recorded decisions only, with sources |
| `notbydefault scan` | Decision debt: unchecked choices, false claims, expired assumptions |
| `notbydefault ui` | Web UI with the live decision graph |

## Quickstart

```bash
pip install -e .
cp .env.example .env         # add GROQ_API_KEY and GEMINI_API_KEY
notbydefault init demo-app
notbydefault check 21 --project demo-app
notbydefault ui --project demo-app
```

To rebuild the full demo scenario on a throwaway copy:

```bash
python scripts/demo_dataset.py --out .demo-dataset/demo-app --offline
```

## Results

On our own evals, decision detection improved from 0.81 to 1.00 recall over three versions, and pivot detection from 0.67 to 1.00. 472 tests, no network.

## Sponsor tools

- **neatlogs:** every model call, verifier and hook traced as spans with tokens and cost.
  - Model calls go to Groq and Google AI Studio over HTTPS. Your project data (notes, cases, code paths) is sent to those providers as prompts. No calls to Anthropic or OpenAI. When `NEATLOGS_API_KEY` is set, prompts and outputs are also sent to neatlogs. When it's not set, no spans leave the machine.
- **Entire:** Entire's Graph finds the callers affected by each decision (so `resolve #21` edits `actions.py` but leaves `app.py` alone — decision #13's own evidence rejected Gemini for summaries). Checkpoints link decisions to the agent session that made them.
- **cfo.ai:** pricing ($49/team/month hypothesis) and a 12-month runway plan in `business/plan.md`.

## Known limitations

- Live demo may require a resume across days when provider free-tier quotas reset; the check saves state and resumes without duplicating requests.
- Eval results are measured on our own cases with held-out cases written before fixes. Not independently labeled.
- `test_hook_is_fast` is a timing flake (300 ms limit); passes when run alone.

## Submission

## Numbers in the README

Every number is typed into the README by hand, which is normal for a README. I checked each one against the data it comes from: the demo dataset that the screenshots use, `eval/results/`, `providers.yaml` and the test collection.

| hook "runs in under 300 ms" | `test_hook_is_fast` took 405 ms in the last full run; your README limitation says it's a flake | ❌ the measurements don't support this as a fact; it's a target |

# NotByDefault

**Prove the choice. Recheck the decision.**

AI coding agents pick models, databases and SDKs by default and give a reason. NotByDefault checks whether that reason is true on your project's own data, records the evidence, and reopens the decision when a requirement, price or fact changes.

> No decision without a why.

## Example

An agent picked `openai/gpt-oss-120b` for an action-items endpoint because it was "cost-effective, strong at extraction, widely used". On the project's 12 cases it scored 10/12 at $407/mo, over the $375 budget. `gemini-3.1-flash-lite` scored 11/12 within budget. `notbydefault resolve 21` switched to it on a branch, with generated tests going from 0/12 to 12/12, and wrote the PR.

When the requirement "data must stay in the EU" was added, that decision was flagged **needs_review** (no documented regional guarantee) and an older Groq decision **stale** (Groq documents US-only). Stale means a known fact breaks it; needs_review means a human should judge.

Trace in neatlogs: `4bcff389ab979638e4ffa7ee88619318`

## How it works

1. **Catch.** A Claude Code `PreToolUse` hook spots a decision when the agent writes a model name, installs an SDK or edits a manifest. It runs in under 300 ms and never blocks the agent.
2. **Record.** The decision, the agent's stated reason and the code it touches go into a decision graph (SQLite, stored with the repo).
3. **Check the reasons.** `claims` splits the reason into cost, quality, latency, compliance and popularity claims, and gives each a verdict with a source. "Widely used" is never evidence for your project.
4. **Check the choice.** `check` runs several candidates on your own cases. Verifiers catch bad outputs, two judges from different model families score them, and confidence intervals flag runs that are too close to call.
5. **Act.** `resolve` applies the winner on a branch (`nbd/<id>-<slug>`), edits only that decision's call sites, generates tests from past failures and writes the PR text. It never touches main or pushes.
6. **Watch.** Each decision stores its assumptions: budget, volume, prices, data region, requirements. `watch` and `require` reopen the affected decisions when any of them change.
7. **Review.** `ui` shows the decision graph, a receipt per decision with its full evidence, a change timeline, eval results and costs. `scan` scores the repo's decision debt (the demo repo scores 14).

## Commands

| Command | What it does |
|---|---|
| `notbydefault check <id>` | Fit-check a decision on your own cases |
| `notbydefault claims <id>` | Verdict on each claim in the agent's reason |
| `notbydefault resolve <id>` | Apply the winner on a branch, with tests and PR text |
| `notbydefault require <project> "<text>"` | Add a requirement; mark decisions stale or needs_review |
| `notbydefault watch` | Reopen decisions whose assumptions changed |
| `notbydefault why "<question>"` | Answer from recorded decisions only, with sources |
| `notbydefault scan` | Decision debt: unchecked choices, false claims, expired assumptions |
| `notbydefault ui` | Web UI with the live decision graph |

## Quickstart

```bash
pip install -e .
cp .env.example .env         # add GROQ_API_KEY and GEMINI_API_KEY
notbydefault init demo-app
notbydefault check 21 --project demo-app
notbydefault ui --project demo-app
```

To rebuild the full demo scenario on a throwaway copy:

```bash
python scripts/demo_dataset.py --out .demo-dataset/demo-app --offline
```

## Results

On our own evals, decision detection improved from 0.81 to 1.00 recall over three versions, and pivot detection from 0.67 to 1.00. 472 tests, no network.

## Sponsor tools

- **neatlogs:** every model call, verifier and hook traced as spans with tokens and cost.
  - Model calls go to Groq and Google AI Studio over HTTPS. Your project data (notes, cases, code paths) is sent to those providers as prompts. No calls to Anthropic or OpenAI. When `NEATLOGS_API_KEY` is set, prompts and outputs are also sent to neatlogs. When it's not set, no spans leave the machine.
- **Entire:** Entire's Graph finds the callers affected by each decision (so `resolve #21` edits `actions.py` but leaves `app.py` alone — decision #13's own evidence rejected Gemini for summaries). Checkpoints link decisions to the agent session that made them.
- **cfo.ai:** pricing ($49/team/month hypothesis) and a 12-month runway plan in `business/plan.md`.

## Known limitations

- Live demo may require a resume across days when provider free-tier quotas reset; the check saves state and resumes without duplicating requests.
- Eval results are measured on our own cases with held-out cases written before fixes. Not independently labeled.
- `test_hook_is_fast` is a timing flake (300 ms limit); passes when run alone.

    p, did = project
    code, report = run(p, did)

input.new_string:
Every run is one neatlogs trace (`fit/tracing.py`): a span per agent step with a `focus_area`, a
span per model and judge call; journals are kept locally when export fails.

**Focus areas.** Every step, event and call carries one of the eight `FOCUS_AREAS` (planning,
tool use, state, context, execution, recovery, verification, iteration); `FOCUS_LABELS` gives
their display names. The check's report prints a step strip (`step_strip`: `plan [planning]  →
preflight [tool_use]  →  ...`), and the UI shows the same strip on the fit-check evidence, an agent
journal with one focus area per entry, and an overview row linking each area to the receipt
section where it shows most (`data.FOCUS_MAP`; a test checks every span listed there is emitted
with its area). Journals saved before the 2026-10-12 retag carry the old tags; `RETAGGED` maps
(name, old tag) to today's tag for display only (`current_focus`), and the badge's tooltip keeps
the recorded one.

**Handled outcomes.** A model call that fails in an expected way the caller handles ends its span
OK with `nbd.outcome` (and `nbd.outcome_reason`) instead of ERROR, so the dashboard's error rate
counts real failures only. `HANDLED_OUTCOMES`: `offline_cache_miss` (`llm.OfflineCacheMiss`: offline
and nothing cached), `daily_limit` (`DailyLimitReached`: the run stops and resumes from the cache),
`preflight_unavailable` (a preflight probe finds a model unavailable and swaps it) and
`judge_fallback` (the same for the judge, which falls back to a second judge, a freed candidate or
reference-only scoring). The exception classes carry their outcome; preflight probes are
recognised by their role. Any other exception still marks the span ERROR with the exception
recorded.

**Net saving.** Below the monthly cost comparison, the report, the decision record's verdict, the
receipt and the resolve PR add one line computed from the results file (`report.net_saving_line`):
today's and the recommended setup's monthly cost at the assumed volume, the difference, the
check's list-price spend, and first-month ROI (saving minus that spend), all from unrounded
values. It is left out when the recommendation saves nothing.

# NotByDefault

**Prove the choice. Recheck the decision.**

AI coding agents pick models, databases and SDKs by default and give a reason. NotByDefault checks whether that reason is true on your project's own data, records the evidence, and reopens the decision when a requirement, price or fact changes.

> No decision without a why.

## Example

An agent picked `openai/gpt-oss-120b` for an action-items endpoint because it was "cost-effective, strong at extraction, widely used". On the project's 12 cases it scored 10/12 at $407/mo, over the $375 budget. `gemini-3.1-flash-lite` scored 11/12 within budget. `notbydefault resolve 21` switched to it on a branch, with generated tests going from 0/12 to 12/12, and wrote the PR.

When the requirement "data must stay in the EU" was added, that decision was flagged **needs_review** (no documented regional guarantee) and an older Groq decision **stale** (Groq documents US-only). Stale means a known fact breaks it; needs_review means a human should judge.

Trace in neatlogs: `4bcff389ab979638e4ffa7ee88619318`

## How it works

1. **Catch.** A Claude Code `PreToolUse` hook spots a decision when the agent writes a model name, installs an SDK or edits a manifest. It targets under 300 ms (p50 under 200 ms; worst case 405 ms under full-suite load) and never blocks the agent.
2. **Record.** The decision, the agent's stated reason and the code it touches go into a decision graph (SQLite, stored with the repo).
3. **Check the reasons.** `claims` splits the reason into cost, quality, latency, compliance and popularity claims, and gives each a verdict with a source. "Widely used" is never evidence for your project.
4. **Check the choice.** `check` runs several candidates on your own cases. Verifiers catch bad outputs, two judges from different model families score them, and confidence intervals flag runs that are too close to call.
5. **Act.** `resolve` applies the winner on a branch (`nbd/<id>-<slug>`), edits only that decision's call sites, generates tests from past failures and writes the PR text. It never touches main or pushes.
6. **Watch.** Each decision stores its assumptions: budget, volume, prices, data region, requirements. `watch` and `require` reopen the affected decisions when any of them change.
7. **Review.** `ui` shows the decision graph, a receipt per decision with its full evidence, a change timeline, eval results and costs. `scan` scores the repo's decision debt (the demo repo scores 14).

## Commands

| Command | What it does |
|---|---|
| `notbydefault check <id>` | Fit-check a decision on your own cases |
| `notbydefault claims <id>` | Verdict on each claim in the agent's reason |
| `notbydefault resolve <id>` | Apply the winner on a branch, with tests and PR text |
| `notbydefault require <project> "<text>"` | Add a requirement; mark decisions stale or needs_review |
| `notbydefault watch` | Reopen decisions whose assumptions changed |
| `notbydefault why "<question>"` | Answer from recorded decisions only, with sources |
| `notbydefault scan` | Decision debt: unchecked choices, false claims, expired assumptions |
| `notbydefault ui` | Web UI with the live decision graph |

## Quickstart

```bash
pip install -e .
cp .env.example .env         # add GROQ_API_KEY and GEMINI_API_KEY
notbydefault init demo-app
notbydefault check 21 --project demo-app
notbydefault ui --project demo-app
```

To rebuild the full demo scenario on a throwaway copy:

```bash
python scripts/demo_dataset.py --out .demo-dataset/demo-app --offline
```

## Results

On our own evals, decision detection improved from 0.81 to 1.00 recall over three versions. Pivot recall 0.67 → 1.00 on original cases; 0.5 on held-out cases (v2 and v3). We ship with the lower number visible — held-out is where the next version has to improve. 472 tests, no network.

## Sponsor tools

- **neatlogs:** every model call, verifier and hook traced as spans with tokens and cost.
  - Model calls go to Groq and Google AI Studio over HTTPS. Your project data (notes, cases, code paths) is sent to those providers as prompts. No calls to Anthropic or OpenAI. When `NEATLOGS_API_KEY` is set, prompts and outputs are also sent to neatlogs. When it's not set, no spans leave the machine.
- **Entire:** Entire's Graph finds the callers affected by each decision (so `resolve #21` edits `actions.py` but leaves `app.py` alone — decision #13's own evidence rejected Gemini for summaries). Checkpoints link decisions to the agent session that made them.
- **cfo.ai:** pricing ($49/team/month hypothesis) and a 12-month runway plan in `business/plan.md`.

## Known limitations

- Live demo may require a resume across days when provider free-tier quotas reset; the check saves state and resumes without duplicating requests.
- Eval results are measured on our own cases with held-out cases written before fixes. Not independently labeled.
- `test_hook_is_fast` is a timing flake (300 ms limit); passes when run alone.

## Submission

neatHack, October 10-12, 2026 · solo, [@Mischa0099](https://github.com/Mischa0099) · Demo video: _link after upload_

# NotByDefault — Business plan

Generated with cfo.ai's Ari agent on 2026-10-12 using business/costs.csv.

## Pricing (launch hypothesis, not validated)

| Tier | Price | Included |
|---|---|---|
| Starter | $49/team/mo | Unlimited collaborators, 4 bounded fit-checks/mo |
| Growth | $149/team/mo | 20 fit-checks/mo, ongoing decision monitoring |

Priced per team because the value is reviewing decisions, not counting engineers. One persistent $62/mo saved decision covers Starter with $13 left over.

## Unit economics

LLM cost at list price: $0.1148/customer/month (currently $0 paid, free tier).
Contribution margin after modeled payment fees: 99.6% – 99.9% across tiers.

## 12-month runway (revised, 2026-10-12)

Starting cash: $5,000. Draw: $0 Nov–Apr, $2,000/mo May–Oct.

Three customer streams:
- Two pilots paying $49 from November (upfront, hand-sold).
- Acquisition forecast: 5 → 35 qualified prospects/mo, 20% conversion, 3% monthly churn.
- Upgrades: 20% of surviving customers move to $149 Growth in their third paid month.

Growth customers carry the higher 20 fit-checks/mo usage cost. $150/mo operating reserve included.

| | |
|---|---|
| Starting cash | $5,000 |
| Lowest month-end cash | $4,649 (August 2027) |
| Ending cash (October 2027) | $5,354 |
| October 2027 MRR | $2,789 |
| Additional cash required | $0 |

Cash builds to ~$7,000 by April, declines after draws start in May, recovers in September as monthly cash flow turns positive.

- Pricing is a launch hypothesis, not a validated price.
- Upgrade rate (20% in month 3) is an assumption; the plan has not been tested against zero upgrades.
- Living costs covered by $2,000/mo draw are modest — most founders need more.
- Demo evidence is one decision on one app, not a typical-customer ROI.
- Taxes, substantial delivery labor, usage spikes excluded.
- The $5,000 starting cash is assumed to be self-funded; no outside funding modelled.

# NotByDefault

**Prove the choice. Recheck the decision.**

AI coding agents pick models, databases and SDKs by default and give a reason. NotByDefault checks whether that reason is true on your project's own data, records the evidence, and reopens the decision when a requirement, price or fact changes.

> No decision without a why.

## Example

An agent picked `openai/gpt-oss-120b` for an action-items endpoint because it was "cost-effective, strong at extraction, widely used". On the project's 12 cases it scored 10/12 at $407/mo, over the $375 budget. `gemini-3.1-flash-lite` scored 11/12 within budget. `notbydefault resolve 21` switched to it on a branch, with generated tests going from 0/12 to 12/12, and wrote the PR.

When the requirement "data must stay in the EU" was added, that decision was flagged **needs_review** (no documented regional guarantee) and an older Groq decision **stale** (Groq documents US-only). Stale means a known fact breaks it; needs_review means a human should judge.

Trace in neatlogs: `4bcff389ab979638e4ffa7ee88619318`

## How it works

1. **Catch.** A Claude Code `PreToolUse` hook spots a decision when the agent writes a model name, installs an SDK or edits a manifest. It targets under 300 ms (p50 under 200 ms; worst case 405 ms under full-suite load) and never blocks the agent.
2. **Record.** The decision, the agent's stated reason and the code it touches go into a decision graph (SQLite, stored with the repo).
3. **Check the reasons.** `claims` splits the reason into cost, quality, latency, compliance and popularity claims, and gives each a verdict with a source. "Widely used" is never evidence for your project.
4. **Check the choice.** `check` runs several candidates on your own cases. Verifiers catch bad outputs, two judges from different model families score them, and confidence intervals flag runs that are too close to call.
5. **Act.** `resolve` applies the winner on a branch (`nbd/<id>-<slug>`), edits only that decision's call sites, generates tests from past failures and writes the PR text. It never touches main or pushes.
6. **Watch.** Each decision stores its assumptions: budget, volume, prices, data region, requirements. `watch` and `require` reopen the affected decisions when any of them change.
7. **Review.** `ui` shows the decision graph, a receipt per decision with its full evidence, a change timeline, eval results and costs. `scan` scores the repo's decision debt (the demo repo scores 14).

## Commands

| Command | What it does |
|---|---|
| `notbydefault check <id>` | Fit-check a decision on your own cases |
| `notbydefault claims <id>` | Verdict on each claim in the agent's reason |
| `notbydefault resolve <id>` | Apply the winner on a branch, with tests and PR text |
| `notbydefault require <project> "<text>"` | Add a requirement; mark decisions stale or needs_review |
| `notbydefault watch` | Reopen decisions whose assumptions changed |
| `notbydefault why "<question>"` | Answer from recorded decisions only, with sources |
| `notbydefault scan` | Decision debt: unchecked choices, false claims, expired assumptions |
| `notbydefault ui` | Web UI with the live decision graph |

## Quickstart

```bash
pip install -e .
cp .env.example .env         # add GROQ_API_KEY and GEMINI_API_KEY
notbydefault init demo-app
notbydefault check 21 --project demo-app
notbydefault ui --project demo-app
```

To rebuild the full demo scenario on a throwaway copy:

```bash
python scripts/demo_dataset.py --out .demo-dataset/demo-app --offline
```

## Results

On our own evals, decision detection improved from 0.81 to 1.00 recall over three versions. Pivot recall 0.67 → 1.00 on original cases; 0.5 on held-out cases (v2 and v3). We ship with the lower number visible — held-out is where the next version has to improve. 474 tests, no network.

## Sponsor tools

- **neatlogs:** every model call, verifier and hook traced as spans with tokens and cost.
  - Model calls go to Groq and Google AI Studio over HTTPS. Your project data (notes, cases, code paths) is sent to those providers as prompts. No calls to Anthropic or OpenAI. When `NEATLOGS_API_KEY` is set, prompts and outputs are also sent to neatlogs. When it's not set, no spans leave the machine.
- **Entire:** Entire's Graph finds the callers affected by each decision (so `resolve #21` edits `actions.py` but leaves `app.py` alone — decision #13's own evidence rejected Gemini for summaries). Checkpoints link decisions to the agent session that made them.
- **cfo.ai:** pricing ($49/team/month hypothesis) and a 12-month runway plan in `business/plan.md`.

## Known limitations

- Live demo may require a resume across days when provider free-tier quotas reset; the check saves state and resumes without duplicating requests.
- Eval results are measured on our own cases with held-out cases written before fixes. Not independently labeled.
- `test_hook_is_fast` is a timing flake (300 ms limit); passes when run alone.

## Submission

def step_recommend(self, error) -> None:
        from notbydefault.fit.providers import load_catalog, split_id
        v = self.results["verdict"]
        cfg = self.results["config"]
        stats = self.results["stats"]
        current = stats.get(cfg["chosen"]) or {}
        model, setup = v["recommended"]
        self._say(f"  verdict: {v['kind']}: {v['summary']}")
        if v["kind"] == "keep":
            raise Stop(0, f"Recommendation: keep {cfg['chosen']}; nothing to change.")
        if v["kind"] != "switch":
            raise Stop(2, "Recommendation: none (the fit check had too little evidence); rerun "
                          f"`notbydefault check {self.decision_id}` with more cases. Nothing changed.")
        if setup != "alone":
            raise Stop(2, f"Recommendation: {model} with a verifier and retries; adding a verifier "
                          "loop to the code is not automated yet. Nothing changed.")
        rec = stats[model]
        catalog = getattr(self.client, "catalog", None) or load_catalog(self.project)
        providers = catalog.get("providers") or {}
        old, new = split_id(cfg["chosen"]), split_id(model)
        self.target, self.old_target = model, cfg["chosen"]
        self.branch = branch_name(self.decision_id, model)
        edits, by_file = [], {}
        for s in self.inv["sites"]:
            by_file.setdefault(s.path, []).append(s)
        for path, sites in by_file.items():
            if not path.endswith(".py"):
                raise EditError(f"{path}: only Python call sites can be edited automatically")
            before = read_raw(self.project / path)
            after, notes = edit_file(before, path, sites, old, new, providers)
            edits.append(FileEdit(path, before, after, [s.describe() for s in sites], notes))
        self.edits = edits
        self.providers = providers
        self._plan_tests(old, new)
        self._say(f"\nRecommend: switch {cfg['chosen']} -> {model}")
        self._say(f"  correct {correct_text(rec)}, hard {hard_text(rec)}, "
                  f"verifier pass {rec['pass_rate']:.0%}, "
                  f"${rec['monthly_cost']:.2f}/month vs ${current.get('monthly_cost', 0):.2f}, "
                  f"latency {rec['avg_latency_s']:.1f}s vs {current.get('avg_latency_s', 0):.1f}s "
                  "per call")
        for s, o in self.inv["excluded"]:
            warn = (f"; its own fit check REJECTED {model}" if model in o["rejects"] else "")
            self._say(f"  not changing {s.describe()}: it is decision #{o['id']}'s call site{warn}")
        if old[0] != new[0]:
            self._say(f"  provider changes {old[0]} -> {new[0]}: deployments need "
                      f"{providers[new[0]]['key_env']} set")
        self._say("")
        for e in edits:
            self._say(e.diff().rstrip("\n"))
            for n in e.notes:
                self._say(f"  ({n})")
        g = self.gen
        if g["skipped"]:
            self._say(f"\nGenerated tests: none ({g['skipped']})")
        else:
            self._say(f"\nGenerated tests: {len(g['cases'])} case(s) ({g['from_bank']} from the "
                      f"failure bank, {len(g['cases']) - g['from_bank']} reference) x "
                      f"{len(g['sites'])} call site(s) -> {g['path']}; run before and after the "
                      "edit")
            for path, names in g["whole_file"].items():
                self._say(f"  Entire off: {path} is one site; testing the {len(names)} "
                          f"function(s) in it that call the model: {', '.join(names)}")
        self.tracer.event("recommendation", "planning", f"switch {cfg['chosen']} -> {model}",
                          files=[e.path for e in edits], branch=self.branch)
        if not self.opts.apply:
            raise Stop(0, f"\nDry run: nothing changed. Re-run with --apply to make these edits on "
                          f"branch {self.branch}.")
        if not self.opts.yes and not self._ask_yes(
                f"\nApply on a new branch {self.branch}? [y/N] "):
            raise Stop(1, "Not approved; nothing changed.")

def resolve(p: Path, did: int, client, apply: bool) -> None:
    from notbydefault.fit.tracing import make_tracer
    from notbydefault.resolve import Resolver, ResolveOptions
    client.step = f"resolve {did}{' --apply' if apply else ''}"
    lines: list[str] = []
    r = Resolver(p, did, ResolveOptions(apply=apply, yes=apply),
                 tracer=make_tracer(f"demo-resolve-{did}"),
                 ask=lambda q: "y", out=lines.append, client=client)
    code = r.run()
    print("\n".join(lines) + f"\n(exit {code})")
    if r.tracer.trace_id:
        traces.append((client.step, r.tracer.trace_id))
        print(f"[trace] {client.step}: {r.tracer.trace_id}")

def main() -> int:
    ap = argparse.ArgumentParser(description=__doc__.split("\n\n")[0])
    ap.add_argument("--out", default=str(REPO / ".demo-dataset" / "demo-app"),
                    help="the copy to (re)build (default .demo-dataset/demo-app)")
    ap.add_argument("--decision", type=int, default=21, help="decision to resolve (default 21)")
    ap.add_argument("--offline", action="store_true",
                    help="no provider calls: answer from the response cache or fall back")
    ap.add_argument("--fresh", action="store_true",
                    help="don't reuse the previous build's model-response cache")
    ap.add_argument("--no-shots", action="store_true", help="don't regenerate docs/screenshots")
    args = ap.parse_args()
    for stream in (sys.stdout, sys.stderr):
        stream.reconfigure(errors="replace", line_buffering=True)
    from notbydefault.claims import run as claims_run
    from notbydefault.env import load_env
    from notbydefault.scan import scan
    from notbydefault.stale import require
    from notbydefault.watch import watch
    load_env()

    p = copy_demo(Path(args.out).resolve(), args.fresh)
    say(f"copy ready: {p} (git repo on main)")
    client = providers(p, args.offline)
    with Step(p, "0. watch (baseline)"):
        captured("watch (baseline)", watch, p)
    with Step(p, "1. agent reasons (scripted, labelled as such)"):
        reasoned = record_reasons(p)
    with Step(p, f"2a. resolve {args.decision} (dry run)"):
        resolve(p, args.decision, client, apply=False)
    with Step(p, f"2b. resolve {args.decision} --apply (on the copy's branch; commit answered yes)"):
        resolve(p, args.decision, client, apply=True)
    with Step(p, "3. pivot"):
        pivot(p, client)
    with Step(p, "3b. agent turn: digest.py"):
        new_id = agent_turn(p)
    first = [args.decision] if args.decision in reasoned else []
    for did in first + [d for d in reasoned if d != args.decision] + [new_id] * bool(new_id):
        with Step(p, f"4. claims {did}"):
            client.step = f"claims {did}"
            captured(f"claims {did}", claims_run, p, did, client=client)
    with Step(p, f'5. require "{REQUIREMENT}"'):
        client.step = "require"
        captured("require", require, p, REQUIREMENT, client=client)
    with Step(p, "6. watch"):
        captured("watch", watch, p)
    with Step(p, "7. scan"):
        captured("scan", scan, p)
    shots = 0
    if not args.no_shots:
        with Step(p, "8. screenshots -> docs/screenshots (light + dark)"):
            shots = screenshots(p, args.decision, new_id)

    say("summary")
    print("trace ids created:")
    for step, t in traces:
        print(f"  {step:<28} {t}")
    if not traces:
        print("  none (telemetry off)")
    print(f"files written: {len(dict.fromkeys(written))}")
    print(f"provider calls made: {client.requests_made}, answered from cache: {client.cache_hits}")
    print(f"\nDataset: {p}\nUI:      python -m notbydefault ui --project \"{p}\"")
    if shots:
        print(f"screenshots failed (exit {shots})")
    return shots


if __name__ == "__main__":
    sys.exit(main())

# NotByDefault

**Prove the choice. Recheck the decision.**

AI coding agents pick models, databases and SDKs by default and give a reason. NotByDefault checks whether that reason is true on your project's own data, records the evidence, and reopens the decision when a requirement, price or fact changes.

> No decision without a why.

## Example

An agent picked `openai/gpt-oss-120b` for an action-items endpoint because it was "cost-effective, strong at extraction, widely used". On the project's 12 cases it scored 10/12 at $407/mo, over the $375 budget. `gemini-3.1-flash-lite` scored 11/12 within budget. `notbydefault resolve 21` switched to it on a branch, with generated tests going from 0/12 to 12/12, and wrote the PR.

When the requirement "data must stay in the EU" was added, that decision was flagged **needs_review** (no documented regional guarantee) and an older Groq decision **stale** (Groq documents US-only). Stale means a known fact breaks it; needs_review means a human should judge.

Trace in neatlogs: `4bcff389ab979638e4ffa7ee88619318`

## How it works

1. **Catch.** A Claude Code `PreToolUse` hook spots a decision when the agent writes a model name, installs an SDK or edits a manifest. It targets under 300 ms (p50 under 200 ms; worst case 405 ms under full-suite load) and never blocks the agent.
2. **Record.** The decision, the agent's stated reason and the code it touches go into a decision graph (SQLite, stored with the repo).
3. **Check the reasons.** `claims` splits the reason into cost, quality, latency, compliance and popularity claims, and gives each a verdict with a source. "Widely used" is never evidence for your project.
4. **Check the choice.** `check` runs several candidates on your own cases. Verifiers catch bad outputs, two judges from different model families score them, and confidence intervals flag runs that are too close to call.
5. **Act.** `resolve` applies the winner on a branch (`nbd/<id>-<slug>`), edits only that decision's call sites, generates tests from past failures and writes the PR text. It never touches main or pushes.
6. **Watch.** Each decision stores its assumptions: budget, volume, prices, data region, requirements. `watch` and `require` reopen the affected decisions when any of them change.
7. **Review.** `ui` shows the decision graph, a receipt per decision with its full evidence, a change timeline, eval results and costs. `scan` scores the repo's decision debt (the demo repo scores 14).

## Commands

| Command | What it does |
|---|---|
| `notbydefault check <id>` | Fit-check a decision on your own cases |
| `notbydefault claims <id>` | Verdict on each claim in the agent's reason |
| `notbydefault resolve <id>` | Apply the winner on a branch, with tests and PR text |
| `notbydefault require <project> "<text>"` | Add a requirement; mark decisions stale or needs_review |
| `notbydefault watch` | Reopen decisions whose assumptions changed |
| `notbydefault why "<question>"` | Answer from recorded decisions only, with sources |
| `notbydefault scan` | Decision debt: unchecked choices, false claims, expired assumptions |
| `notbydefault ui` | Web UI with the live decision graph |

## Quickstart

```bash
pip install -e .
cp .env.example .env         # add GROQ_API_KEY and GEMINI_API_KEY
notbydefault init demo-app
notbydefault check 21 --project demo-app
notbydefault ui --project demo-app
```

To rebuild the full demo scenario on a throwaway copy:

```bash
python scripts/demo_dataset.py --out .demo-dataset/demo-app --offline
```

## Results

On our own evals, decision detection improved from 0.81 to 1.00 recall over three versions. Pivot recall 0.67 → 1.00 on original cases; 0.5 on held-out cases (v2 and v3). We ship with the lower number visible — held-out is where the next version has to improve. 474 tests, no network.

## Sponsor tools

- **neatlogs:** every model call, verifier and hook traced as spans with tokens and cost.
  - Model calls go to Groq and Google AI Studio over HTTPS. Your project data (notes, cases, code paths) is sent to those providers as prompts. No calls to Anthropic or OpenAI. When `NEATLOGS_API_KEY` is set, prompts and outputs are also sent to neatlogs. When it's not set, no spans leave the machine.
- **Entire:** Entire's Graph finds the callers affected by each decision (so `resolve #21` edits `actions.py` but leaves `app.py` alone — decision #13's own evidence rejected Gemini for summaries). Checkpoints link decisions to the agent session that made them.
- **cfo.ai:** Pricing modeled with Ari (cfo.ai): $49/team/month Starter, $149/month Growth. Revised base case is self-funded through October 2027 under disclosed assumptions. Full plan: `business/plan.md`.

## Business case

NotByDefault reviews AI coding agents' technical choices against the project's own data and checks their stated reasoning, with proposed launch pricing of $49 per team per month. In our demo, one model-selection decision reduced projected inference costs by $62/month while improving accuracy on the project's own cases — enough to cover the subscription if those savings persist. Our revised 12-month plan starts with $5,000 of founder cash, two pre-launch pilot customers at $49, 20% upgrade to $149 Growth in the third paid month, and a staged founder draw ($0 Nov–Apr, $2k/mo May–Oct) — resulting in a self-funded year with ~$5,354 ending cash and $2,789 MRR by October 2027 under disclosed assumptions.

## Known limitations

- Live demo may require a resume across days when provider free-tier quotas reset; the check saves state and resumes without duplicating requests.
- Eval results are measured on our own cases with held-out cases written before fixes. Not independently labeled.
- `test_hook_is_fast` is a timing flake (300 ms limit); passes when run alone.

## Submission

On our own evals, decision detection improved from 0.81 to 1.00 recall over three versions. Pivot recall 0.67 → 1.00 on original cases; 0.5 on held-out cases (v2 and v3). We ship with the lower number visible — held-out is where the next version has to improve. 474 tests, no network.

## Sponsor tools

- **neatlogs:** every model call, verifier and hook traced as spans with tokens and cost.
  - Model calls go to Groq and Google AI Studio over HTTPS. Your project data (notes, cases, code paths) is sent to those providers as prompts. No calls to Anthropic or OpenAI. When `NEATLOGS_API_KEY` is set, prompts and outputs are also sent to neatlogs. When it's not set, no spans leave the machine.
- **Entire:** Entire's Graph finds the callers affected by each decision (so `resolve #21` edits `actions.py` but leaves `app.py` alone — decision #13's own evidence rejected Gemini for summaries). Checkpoints link decisions to the agent session that made them.
- **cfo.ai:** Pricing modeled with Ari (cfo.ai): $49/team/month Starter, $149/month Growth. Revised base case is self-funded through October 2027 under disclosed assumptions. Full plan: `business/plan.md`.

## Business case

NotByDefault reviews AI coding agents' technical choices against the project's own data and checks their stated reasoning, with proposed launch pricing of $49 per team per month. In our demo, one model-selection decision reduced projected inference costs by $62/month while improving accuracy on the project's own cases — enough to cover the subscription if those savings persist. Our revised 12-month plan starts with $5,000 of founder cash, two pre-launch pilot customers at $49, 20% upgrade to $149 Growth in the third paid month, and a staged founder draw ($0 Nov–Apr, $2k/mo May–Oct) — resulting in a self-funded year with ~$5,354 ending cash and $2,789 MRR by October 2027 under disclosed assumptions.

## Known limitations

- Live demo may require a resume across days when provider free-tier quotas reset; the check saves state and resumes without duplicating requests.
- Eval results are measured on our own cases with held-out cases written before fixes. Not independently labeled.
- `test_hook_is_fast` is a timing flake (300 ms limit); passes when run alone.

# NotByDefault — Business plan

Generated with cfo.ai's Ari agent on 2026-10-12 using business/costs.csv.

## Pricing (launch hypothesis, not validated)

| Tier | Price | Included |
|---|---|---|
| Starter | $49/team/mo | Unlimited collaborators, 4 bounded fit-checks/mo |
| Growth | $149/team/mo | 20 fit-checks/mo, ongoing decision monitoring |

Priced per team because the value is reviewing decisions, not counting engineers. One persistent $62/mo saved decision covers Starter with $13 left over.

## Unit economics

LLM cost at list price: $0.1148/customer/month (currently $0 paid, free tier).
Contribution margin after modeled payment fees: 99.6% – 99.9% across tiers.

## 12-month runway (revised, 2026-10-12)

Starting cash: $5,000. Draw: $0 Nov–Apr, $2,000/mo May–Oct.

Three customer streams:
- Two pilots paying $49 from November (upfront, hand-sold).
- Acquisition forecast: 5 → 35 qualified prospects/mo, 20% conversion, 3% monthly churn.
- Upgrades: 20% of surviving customers move to $149 Growth in their third paid month.

Growth customers carry the higher 20 fit-checks/mo usage cost. $150/mo operating reserve included.

| | |
|---|---|
| Starting cash | $5,000 |
| Lowest month-end cash | $4,649 (August 2027) |
| Ending cash (October 2027) | $5,354 |
| October 2027 MRR | $2,789 |
| Additional cash required | $0 |

Cash builds to ~$7,000 by April, declines after draws start in May, recovers in September as monthly cash flow turns positive.

## Honest caveats

- Pricing is a launch hypothesis, not a validated price.
- Upgrade rate (20% in month 3) is an assumption; the plan has not been tested against zero upgrades.
- Living costs covered by $2,000/mo draw are modest — most founders need more.
- Demo evidence is one decision on one app, not a typical-customer ROI.
- Taxes, substantial delivery labor, usage spikes excluded.
- The $5,000 starting cash is assumed to be self-funded; no outside funding modelled.

## First experiment (next 30 days)

Offer 10 qualified founders / staff engineers: *"one decision review on your real workload + 30 days monitoring, $49 upfront."* Same offer for all. Deliver manually where needed.

Success gate: ≥ 3/10 pay, ≥ 2/10 renew at $49 after 30 days.

Everything now uses the live run's numbers, apart from a few points below where your plan didn't match the code or data. The full suite passes serially (474 tests). Everything is staged, `msg.txt` is written without Co-Authored-By, and nothing is committed.

**What the live run says, which the README now follows:**

| Setup | Correct | Hard | Monthly | Within $375 budget? |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| gpt-oss-120b (today) | 10/12 | 6/8 | $418.04 | no |
| gpt-oss-20b + verifier (recommended) | 10/12 | 6/8 | $336.48 | yes |
| gemini-3.1-flash-lite (best quality in budget) | 11/12 | 8/8 | $345.07 | yes |

The saving is $81.56/mo, and the live trace is `0f65667e9f5c521dfc124c89f188f9ca`.

**Where I didn't follow your text:**
- **Resolve:** the demo now records `resolve`'s real answer, as you chose. It recommends gpt-oss-20b + verifier and stops, because adding a verifier loop isn't automated yet. The README no longer says "resolve applied…" or "generated tests 0/12 → 12/12".
- **Gemini is within budget:** gemini-3.1-flash-lite alone costs $345/mo, under the $375 budget, so the README says that rather than "over budget". Your caveat paragraph went in word for word.
- **Business case accuracy:** "improving accuracy" was no longer true. The recommended setup scores 10/12, the same as today, so it now says "at the same accuracy on the project's own cases (10/12)", with $82/month.
- **EU requirement:** #21 and #13 both go stale, because both run on Groq. #13 isn't on Gemini. MongoDB (#7) is the needs_review case.
- **`plan.md`:** the "In our demo…" sentence you quoted isn't in the plan. Its $62 was in the Starter line, which now reads "$82/mo saved decision covers Starter with $33 left over". Your dated update line is added below it.
- **ARCHITECTURE.md:** it had no "Measured" section, so I added one under "Live demo run" with the live numbers. I also corrected the demo-dataset paragraph, which still described #21 on Gemini.

**Things to know before you commit:**
- **The receipt shows two spend figures.** It says "Spent $0.0221 · 15 requests, 56 cache hits", and the net-saving line uses $0.0221. That's because the results file only counts the attempt that finished. The README and `docs/demo.md` use $0.0461, the list price of all 71 live requests. I can make the results file add up both attempts if you want one figure everywhere.
- **The plan's LLM cost input is now out of date.** Regenerating `business/costs.*` from the live results lowers our LLM cost per customer from $0.1148 to $0.0863/month. `plan.md` still cites $0.1148 as its input. I didn't touch that, since you said Ari's numbers don't need re-running.
- **Claim checks used the keyword fallback.** The offline rebuild couldn't reuse the cached model answers, so #21's receipt now says "split by keywords". The verdicts are what you wanted: cost false, quality false ("10/12 vs 11/12 at gemini-3.1-flash-lite, within budget"), popularity untested.
- **What I staged:** the live run's own outputs, `docs/demo.md` and #21's decision record with its two live-run lines.
- **Not staged:** `demo-live-run.txt`.
- **Left unchanged:** `eval/results/v3.json` keeps the old trace id because it's a historical eval record.

def record_live_run(cache: Path | None, attempts: list[dict], trace_id: str, results_rel: str,
                    pricing, out=print) -> float:
    """Write a finished live run's evidence: its total spend into the results file
    (`live_run`, which the report, receipt and PR read), the docs/demo.md line, and the
    decision record's net-saving, cost and run lines (replaced when already there).
    `cache` is the live cache, or None when the shared cache was reused. Returns the spend."""
    from notbydefault.fit.report import net_saving_line, spend_note
    from notbydefault.graph import Graph
    from notbydefault.records import existing_path

    results_path = PROJECT / results_rel
    results = json.loads(results_path.read_text(encoding="utf-8"))
    # a live cache holds exactly the requests this live run made, across every attempt
    entries = cache_entries(cache) if cache else []
    spent = (sum(pricing.prices[e["model"]].cost(e["input_tokens"], e["output_tokens"])
                 for e in entries if e.get("model") in pricing.prices)
             if cache else float(results.get("spent") or 0))
    tries = max(len(attempts), 1)
    if cache:
        results["live_run"] = {"spent": round(spent, 6), "attempts": tries,
                               "requests": len(entries), "cache": cache.name,
                               "traces": [a["trace_id"] for a in attempts]}
        results_path.write_text(json.dumps(results, indent=1, default=str), encoding="utf-8")
        out(f"spent:     {spend_note(spent, tries)}: list price of the {len(entries)} live "
            f"requests in {cache.name}")

    entry = f"live-run trace: {trace_id} ({spend_note(spent, tries)})"
    doc = DEMO_DOC.read_text(encoding="utf-8") if DEMO_DOC.exists() else "# Demo\n"
    doc = LINE.sub(entry, doc, count=1) if LINE.search(doc) else doc.rstrip("\n") + f"\n\n{entry}\n"
    DEMO_DOC.write_text(doc, encoding="utf-8")
    print(f"{DEMO_DOC.relative_to(REPO)}: {entry}")

    # on free-tier keys the cost is the list price of the requests made, not what was billed
    free_tier = (results.get("pricing") or {}).get("free_tier")
    notes = [f"Live-run cost: {spend_note(spent, tries)}, "
             + ("list price of real requests" if free_tier else "real spend")
             + (", fresh cache" if cache else ", response cache reused")
             + ("; free tier, not billed" if free_tier else "") + "."]
    if cache:
        models = {e.get("model") for e in entries}
        days = {datetime.fromisoformat(e["at"]).astimezone().date() for e in entries if e.get("at")}
        many = len(days) != 1
        where = f"across {len(days)} calendar day{'s' * many}" if many else "in 1 calendar day"
        if len(attempts) > 1:
            partial = ", ".join(a["trace_id"] for a in attempts[:-1])
            notes.append(f"Live run: {len(entries)} requests on {len(models)} models {where} "
                         f"(quota reset between). Partial trace: {partial}, final trace: {trace_id}.")
        else:
            notes.append(f"Live run: {len(entries)} requests on {len(models)} models {where}. "
                         f"Trace: {trace_id}.")
    with Graph.for_project(PROJECT) as g:
        decision = g.get_node(DECISION)
    record = existing_path(PROJECT, decision)
    if not record:
        print(f"No decision record for #{DECISION}; not written: " + " / ".join(notes))
        return spent
    st = {(s["model"], s["setup"]): s for s in results["stats"].values()}
    v = results["verdict"]
    cur, rec = (st.get(tuple(v.get(k) or ())) or {} for k in ("reference", "recommended"))
    saving = net_saving_line(cur.get("monthly_cost"), rec.get("monthly_cost"), spent, tries)
    kept = [l for l in record.read_text(encoding="utf-8").rstrip("\n").splitlines()
            if not l.startswith(("Live-run cost:", "Live run:"))]
    if saving:
        kept = [saving if l.startswith("Net saving:") else l for l in kept]
    while kept and not kept[-1].strip():
        kept.pop()
    record.write_text("\n".join(kept) + "\n\n" + "\n".join(notes) + "\n", encoding="utf-8")
    for n in ([saving] if saving else []) + notes:
        print(f"{record.relative_to(REPO)}: {n}")
    return spent

# NotByDefault

**Prove the choice. Recheck the decision.**

AI coding agents pick models, databases and SDKs by default and give a reason. NotByDefault checks whether that reason is true on your project's own data, records the evidence, and reopens the decision when a requirement, price or fact changes.

> No decision without a why.

## Example

An agent picked `openai/gpt-oss-120b` for an action-items endpoint because it was "cost-effective, strong at extraction, widely used". On the project's 12 cases it scored 10/12 at $418/mo, over the $375 budget. The cheapest setup that meets the bar is 10/12 at gpt-oss-20b + verifier, $336/mo: **$418→$336/mo, $81.56/mo saved**. `notbydefault resolve 21` recommends that switch and stops there: adding a verifier loop to the code isn't automated yet, so it changes nothing.

Full comparison between candidates: gpt-oss-20b + verifier is the cheapest in-budget recommendation at $336/mo; gemini-3.1-flash-lite scored higher (11/12 vs 10/12) but $345/mo is still under budget — the ranking depends on whether you prioritize cost or correctness. See the fit-check table.

When the requirement "data must stay in the EU" was added, #21 flipped to **stale** (Groq documents US-only; the chosen stack can't meet the new requirement), and so did an older Groq decision. MongoDB went to **needs_review**: where its data lives depends on how it's deployed. Stale means a known fact breaks it; needs_review means a human should judge.

Live trace in neatlogs: `0f65667e9f5c521dfc124c89f188f9ca` (71 real provider requests across a quota reset, $0.0461 at list price on free tiers).

## How it works

1. **Catch.** A Claude Code `PreToolUse` hook spots a decision when the agent writes a model name, installs an SDK or edits a manifest. It targets under 300 ms (p50 under 200 ms; worst case 405 ms under full-suite load) and never blocks the agent.
2. **Record.** The decision, the agent's stated reason and the code it touches go into a decision graph (SQLite, stored with the repo).
3. **Check the reasons.** `claims` splits the reason into cost, quality, latency, compliance and popularity claims, and gives each a verdict with a source. "Widely used" is never evidence for your project.
4. **Check the choice.** `check` runs several candidates on your own cases. Verifiers catch bad outputs, two judges from different model families score them, and confidence intervals flag runs that are too close to call.
5. **Act.** `resolve` applies the winner on a branch (`nbd/<id>-<slug>`), edits only that decision's call sites, generates tests from past failures and writes the PR text. It never touches main or pushes.
6. **Watch.** Each decision stores its assumptions: budget, volume, prices, data region, requirements. `watch` and `require` reopen the affected decisions when any of them change.
7. **Review.** `ui` shows the decision graph, a receipt per decision with its full evidence, a change timeline, eval results and costs. `scan` scores the repo's decision debt (the demo repo scores 14).

## Commands

| Command | What it does |
|---|---|
| `notbydefault check <id>` | Fit-check a decision on your own cases |
| `notbydefault claims <id>` | Verdict on each claim in the agent's reason |
| `notbydefault resolve <id>` | Apply the winner on a branch, with tests and PR text |
| `notbydefault require <project> "<text>"` | Add a requirement; mark decisions stale or needs_review |
| `notbydefault watch` | Reopen decisions whose assumptions changed |
| `notbydefault why "<question>"` | Answer from recorded decisions only, with sources |
| `notbydefault scan` | Decision debt: unchecked choices, false claims, expired assumptions |
| `notbydefault ui` | Web UI with the live decision graph |

## Quickstart

```bash
pip install -e .
cp .env.example .env         # add GROQ_API_KEY and GEMINI_API_KEY
notbydefault init demo-app
notbydefault check 21 --project demo-app
notbydefault ui --project demo-app
```

To rebuild the full demo scenario on a throwaway copy:

```bash
python scripts/demo_dataset.py --out .demo-dataset/demo-app --offline
```

## Results

On our own evals, decision detection improved from 0.81 to 1.00 recall over three versions. Pivot recall 0.67 → 1.00 on original cases; 0.5 on held-out cases (v2 and v3). We ship with the lower number visible — held-out is where the next version has to improve. 474 tests, no network.

## Sponsor tools

- **neatlogs:** every model call, verifier and hook traced as spans with tokens and cost.
  - Model calls go to Groq and Google AI Studio over HTTPS. Your project data (notes, cases, code paths) is sent to those providers as prompts. No calls to Anthropic or OpenAI. When `NEATLOGS_API_KEY` is set, prompts and outputs are also sent to neatlogs. When it's not set, no spans leave the machine.
- **Entire:** Entire's Graph finds the callers affected by each decision (so `resolve #21` edits `actions.py` but leaves `app.py` alone — decision #13's own evidence rejected Gemini for summaries). Checkpoints link decisions to the agent session that made them.
- **cfo.ai:** Pricing modeled with Ari (cfo.ai): $49/team/month Starter, $149/month Growth. Revised base case is self-funded through October 2027 under disclosed assumptions. Full plan: `business/plan.md`.

## Business case

NotByDefault reviews AI coding agents' technical choices against the project's own data and checks their stated reasoning, with proposed launch pricing of $49 per team per month. In our demo, one model-selection decision reduced projected inference costs by $82/month at the same accuracy on the project's own cases (10/12) — enough to cover the subscription if those savings persist. Our revised 12-month plan starts with $5,000 of founder cash, two pre-launch pilot customers at $49, 20% upgrade to $149 Growth in the third paid month, and a staged founder draw ($0 Nov–Apr, $2k/mo May–Oct) — resulting in a self-funded year with ~$5,354 ending cash and $2,789 MRR by October 2027 under disclosed assumptions.

## Known limitations

- Live demo may require a resume across days when provider free-tier quotas reset; the check saves state and resumes without duplicating requests.
- Eval results are measured on our own cases with held-out cases written before fixes. Not independently labeled.
- `test_hook_is_fast` is a timing flake (300 ms limit); passes when run alone.

# NotByDefault — Business plan

Generated with cfo.ai's Ari agent on 2026-10-12 using business/costs.csv.

## Pricing (launch hypothesis, not validated)

| Tier | Price | Included |
|---|---|---|
| Starter | $49/team/mo | Unlimited collaborators, 4 bounded fit-checks/mo |
| Growth | $149/team/mo | 20 fit-checks/mo, ongoing decision monitoring |

Priced per team because the value is reviewing decisions, not counting engineers. One persistent $82/mo saved decision covers Starter with $33 left over.

Updated 2026-10-12: live run on #21 produced $82/mo saved, not $62. The plan's conclusions are unchanged — more saving per decision strengthens the ROI.

## Unit economics

LLM cost at list price: $0.1148/customer/month (currently $0 paid, free tier).
Contribution margin after modeled payment fees: 99.6% – 99.9% across tiers.

## 12-month runway (revised, 2026-10-12)

Starting cash: $5,000. Draw: $0 Nov–Apr, $2,000/mo May–Oct.

Three customer streams:
- Two pilots paying $49 from November (upfront, hand-sold).

# NotByDefault

**Prove the choice. Recheck the decision.**

AI coding agents pick models, databases and SDKs by default and give a reason. NotByDefault checks whether that reason is true on your project's own data, records the evidence, and reopens the decision when a requirement, price or fact changes.

> No decision without a why.

## Example

An agent picked `openai/gpt-oss-120b` for an action-items endpoint because it was "cost-effective, strong at extraction, widely used". On the project's 12 cases it scored 10/12 at $418/mo, over the $375 budget. The cheapest setup that meets the bar is 10/12 at gpt-oss-20b + verifier, $336/mo: **$418→$336/mo, $81.56/mo saved**. `notbydefault resolve 21` recommends that switch and stops there: adding a verifier loop to the code isn't automated yet, so it changes nothing.

Full comparison between candidates: gpt-oss-20b + verifier is the cheapest in-budget recommendation at $336/mo; gemini-3.1-flash-lite scored higher (11/12 vs 10/12) but $345/mo is still under budget — the ranking depends on whether you prioritize cost or correctness. See the fit-check table.

When the requirement "data must stay in the EU" was added, #21 flipped to **stale** (Groq documents US-only; the chosen stack can't meet the new requirement), and so did an older Groq decision. MongoDB went to **needs_review**: where its data lives depends on how it's deployed. Stale means a known fact breaks it; needs_review means a human should judge.

Live trace in neatlogs: `0f65667e9f5c521dfc124c89f188f9ca` (71 real provider requests across a quota reset, $0.0461 ($0.0461 across two attempts; stop-and-resume saves cached work) at list price on free tiers).

## How it works

1. **Catch.** A Claude Code `PreToolUse` hook spots a decision when the agent writes a model name, installs an SDK or edits a manifest. It targets under 300 ms (p50 under 200 ms; worst case 405 ms under full-suite load) and never blocks the agent.
2. **Record.** The decision, the agent's stated reason and the code it touches go into a decision graph (SQLite, stored with the repo).
3. **Check the reasons.** `claims` splits the reason into cost, quality, latency, compliance and popularity claims, and gives each a verdict with a source. "Widely used" is never evidence for your project.
4. **Check the choice.** `check` runs several candidates on your own cases. Verifiers catch bad outputs, two judges from different model families score them, and confidence intervals flag runs that are too close to call.
5. **Act.** `resolve` applies the winner on a branch (`nbd/<id>-<slug>`), edits only that decision's call sites, generates tests from past failures and writes the PR text. It never touches main or pushes.
6. **Watch.** Each decision stores its assumptions: budget, volume, prices, data region, requirements. `watch` and `require` reopen the affected decisions when any of them change.
7. **Review.** `ui` shows the decision graph, a receipt per decision with its full evidence, a change timeline, eval results and costs. `scan` scores the repo's decision debt (the demo repo scores 14).

## Commands

| Command | What it does |
|---|---|
| `notbydefault check <id>` | Fit-check a decision on your own cases |
| `notbydefault claims <id>` | Verdict on each claim in the agent's reason |
| `notbydefault resolve <id>` | Apply the winner on a branch, with tests and PR text |
| `notbydefault require <project> "<text>"` | Add a requirement; mark decisions stale or needs_review |
| `notbydefault watch` | Reopen decisions whose assumptions changed |
| `notbydefault why "<question>"` | Answer from recorded decisions only, with sources |
| `notbydefault scan` | Decision debt: unchecked choices, false claims, expired assumptions |
| `notbydefault ui` | Web UI with the live decision graph |

## Quickstart

```bash
pip install -e .
cp .env.example .env         # add GROQ_API_KEY and GEMINI_API_KEY
notbydefault init demo-app
notbydefault check 21 --project demo-app
notbydefault ui --project demo-app
```

To rebuild the full demo scenario on a throwaway copy:

```bash
python scripts/demo_dataset.py --out .demo-dataset/demo-app --offline
```

## Results

On our own evals, decision detection improved from 0.81 to 1.00 recall over three versions. Pivot recall 0.67 → 1.00 on original cases; 0.5 on held-out cases (v2 and v3). We ship with the lower number visible — held-out is where the next version has to improve. 474 tests, no network.

## Sponsor tools

- **neatlogs:** every model call, verifier and hook traced as spans with tokens and cost.
  - Model calls go to Groq and Google AI Studio over HTTPS. Your project data (notes, cases, code paths) is sent to those providers as prompts. No calls to Anthropic or OpenAI. When `NEATLOGS_API_KEY` is set, prompts and outputs are also sent to neatlogs. When it's not set, no spans leave the machine.
- **Entire:** Entire's Graph finds the callers affected by each decision (so `resolve #21` edits `actions.py` but leaves `app.py` alone — decision #13's own evidence rejected Gemini for summaries). Checkpoints link decisions to the agent session that made them.
- **cfo.ai:** Pricing modeled with Ari (cfo.ai): $49/team/month Starter, $149/month Growth. Revised base case is self-funded through October 2027 under disclosed assumptions. Full plan: `business/plan.md`.

## Business case

NotByDefault reviews AI coding agents' technical choices against the project's own data and checks their stated reasoning, with proposed launch pricing of $49 per team per month. In our demo, one model-selection decision reduced projected inference costs by $82/month at the same accuracy on the project's own cases (10/12) — enough to cover the subscription if those savings persist. Our revised 12-month plan starts with $5,000 of founder cash, two pre-launch pilot customers at $49, 20% upgrade to $149 Growth in the third paid month, and a staged founder draw ($0 Nov–Apr, $2k/mo May–Oct) — resulting in a self-funded year with ~$5,354 ending cash and $2,789 MRR by October 2027 under disclosed assumptions.

## Known limitations

- Live demo may require a resume across days when provider free-tier quotas reset; the check saves state and resumes without duplicating requests.
- Eval results are measured on our own cases with held-out cases written before fixes. Not independently labeled.
- `test_hook_is_fast` is a timing flake (300 ms limit); passes when run alone.

## Submission

content.text:
The spend now reads $0.0461 with your note everywhere you listed, and the plan has the new LLM cost. The full suite passes serially (475 tests, so the README count is now 475). Everything is staged and `msg.txt` is written; nothing is committed. You'd committed the previous round as `60a13ca`, so this is a separate change set.

**1. One spend figure.** The receipt and net-saving line showed $0.0221 because the results file only counted the attempt that finished. I fixed that from the data rather than editing the figures by hand:
- **Source of the figure:** when a live run finishes, `live_demo_run.py` now records the total over every attempt in the results file. The receipt, the net-saving line and the resolve PR read that total, and fall back to the single attempt's spend when there isn't one.
- **Backfill:** I ran the same function for #21 in both `demo-app` and the demo dataset, using its live cache and `live-run.json`. It made no provider calls, and running it again replaces its lines rather than adding new ones.
- **Result:**
  - Receipt: "Spent $0.0461 ($0.0461 across two attempts; stop-and-resume saves cached work) · 71 live requests".
  - Net-saving line: "Check cost once at $0.0461 (list) ($0.0461 across two attempts; …). First-month ROI: $81.51." The ROI is now $81.56 − $0.0461 instead of $81.56 − $0.0221.
  - The README, ARCHITECTURE, `docs/demo.md` and #21's decision record all carry the same figure and note.
- **Format change:** in `docs/demo.md` the note follows a dash instead of brackets, to avoid "($0.0461 ($0.0461 …))".
- **Screenshots:** I rebuilt the #21 receipt in both themes, plus the fit-check clip. The clip is cut from the same page and would otherwise still show $0.0221.

**2. Plan unit economics.** It now reads "$0.0863/customer/mo on live data (down from $0.1148 in the demo dataset)", with your note that margins and runway conclusions are unchanged. I didn't recompute the 99.6–99.9% margin range, since that came from Ari. The difference is about 3 cents a month on a $49 plan, so the range plausibly still holds.

**Still says $0.0221:** `business/costs.md` lists the #21 check at $0.0221 with 15 requests. That's accurate for the attempt that finished, but the stopped attempt never wrote a results file, so its $0.024 isn't counted in our cost per check. I left it, since it wasn't on your list. If you want, `costs.py` can read the same total.
